News.title: Teens who fled Venezuela after quake disaster are caught up in 7.4-mag Colombia tremor: ‘The earthquake is haunting me’
News.content:
TWO teenage brothers who fled Venezuela after a devastating earthquake have been caught up in another deadly tremor in Colombia.

Deivi Delfín, 15, and his brother Winder, 17, moved to neighbouring Colombia after two back-to-back earthquakes struck in late June.



As they headed home on June 24, quakes measuring 7.2 and 7.5 struck just 39 seconds apart.

Their 12-storey apartment building in La Guaira was reduced to rubble, trapping family members inside.



For the next month, the brothers desperately sifted through the wreckage in search of their loved ones.

Then Deivi spotted a scrap of fabric buried beneath the debris.

The 15-year-old immediately recognised it as part of his grandmother’s floral skirt.

Firefighters later confirmed they had recovered the body of a woman.



Winder then made a heartbreaking discovery of his own when he found his mum, Yusmani, buried beneath a huge slab of concrete.

As rescuers carefully lifted the concrete, they discovered the brothers’ ten-year-old sibling, Moissés, clinging tightly to his mother.

“When his little head fell into my hand, I broke down,” Winder said.

After spending weeks searching for their relatives, Deivi said he and his brother no longer felt like children.

The devastating earthquake killed more than 6,000 people and prompted the brothers to move to Cali, where their father, Deivid, works.



Just three days after arriving in the Colombia’s third largest city, they felt the earth move beneath them once again.

Home to around 2.2 million people, at least 95 people were killed as hundreds of building to rubble.

Deivi was asleep when the tremor began and initially thought he was dreaming.



As the shaking intensified, he jolted upright and raced downstairs, with Winder doing the same.

Outside, the brothers clung to a metal gate as they waited for the violent shaking to stop.

When they finally found their dad outside the barbershop where he worked, they were quick to reassure him.

“Dad, stay calm. We’ve been through this before,” they told him.

“Tears came to my eyes and everything, because I was afraid of what I had already experienced, what my children had experienced,” Deivid said.



“I don’t want anything to happen to my children.”

The 7.4-magnitude quake struck at a depth of around 64 miles in Chocó province and was felt across a vast area of western Colombia.

Tremors were felt hundreds of miles away in Venezuela’s capital Caracas, as well as in Ecuador and Panama.



Officials said 281 people have been confirmed dead and 379 remain missing, with the death toll expected to rise in the coming days

Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella has deployed 1,000 members of the security forces to Cali following reports of looting.

The disaster is an early test for the president, who was inaugurated just days ago on August 7.

On Tuesday, he flew to Pereira with his wife, First Lady Ana Lucía Pineda, to inspect one of the worst-hit areas.

“My commitment is to each and every one of the affected families,” he wrote on X.



“We remain on the ground, working for our people.”

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said America “stands ready to support” Colombia.

The US Department of State described the disaster as “devastating” and pledged £11.5million to provide emergency shelter and supplies.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The EU is also providing funding and supporting rescue operations, foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said.

The Colombian government has meanwhile announced an immediate emergency rent subsidy for people who have lost their homes.

News.title: Second UK train derails just 24 hours after Lewes crash as passengers warned ‘do not travel’ & all trains cancelled
News.content:
A SECOND train has derailed in another major crash just 24 hours after 20 people were injured in Lewes.

Emergency services are responding to reports that a Greater Anglia train derailed just outside of Wickford in Essex.



It comes less than a day after a Southern Rail train crashed and flipped before sliding down an embankment in Lewes, East Sussex, injuring 20 people.

The Greater Anglia train came off the rails at 2.12pm – but it remains unclear if anyone has been seriously injured.



Emergency services have been scrambled to the scene with a local sharing an image of a pair of air ambulances landing near the tracks.

Services between Southend Victoria and Wickford, Essex, are facing major delays to their journey after the train came off the tracks between the two stations.



A Greater Anglia spokesperson said: “Due to a problem currently under investigation between Shenfield and Southend Victoria, all lines are blocked.

“Train services running to and from these stations will be suspended.



“Disruption is expected until further notice.

“Please do not travel between Shenfield and Southend Victoria until further notice.”

Have you been affected by this incident? Email hannah.bentley@thesun.co.uk

It is understood to be the 13.51 service from Wickford to Southend Victoria that came off the tracks.

An image shared to social media appears to show a single carriage at the rear of the train off the tracks and at a dead stop.



A footbridge across the rail line has been closed as crews work at the chaotic scene.

Further images taken by passengers who are reportedly stuck on the stopped train have been shared to social media.

A crowd of stunned bystanders can be seen gathered at the edge of the rails with the crashed train next to them.

All trains in the area have been cancelled as the emergency services work to deal with the scene.

A British Transport Police spokesperson said: “Officers are currently on scene at Wickford railway station in Essex following reports that the rear carriages of a train have derailed in an upright position at 2.12pm today.



“We’re responding alongside paramedics and the fire service. There are currently no reported injuries.”

A National Rail spokesperson said it was dealing with a derailment incident in Anglia.

National Rail added that all lines were blocked between Southend Victoria and Wickford with disruption expected until at least 4.30pm.

A spokesperson said: “We are dealing with a derailment incident in Anglia, and we are working quickly to understand the situation and to provide assistance where needed.

“We will provide further information in due course.”



Local councillor Alex Myers said: “I am aware of reports that a train has derailed in Wickford.

“The footbridge across the line from Salcott Crescent to Russell Gardens is closed and emergency services are in attendance.

“Updates will be provided from the Council, Emergency Services and Greater Anglia as they become available.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“My thoughts are with all those onboard and hope there are no serious injuries.”

Passengers are asked not to travel between Shenfield and Southend Victoria “until further notice”, Greater Anglia said on its website.

News.title: Fears A-level pupils ‘burning pads in BBQs on results day’ sparked wildfire that gutted 19 homes & left 25 in hospital
News.content:
FIRE chiefs are probing whether A-level students celebrating their results by burning notepads may have sparked a huge wildfire that has left 25 in hospital.

A total of 19 homes were completely destroyed and 18 others damaged as families forced to evacuate as the fire spread across Stourbridge, West Midlands, yesterday afternoon.



A-level students across the country had been collecting their final grades – with many celebrating throughout the day.

However, fire chiefs are now reportedly investigating whether teenagers burning notepads and celebrating with barbecues may have been behind the blaze.



A spokesman for West Midlands Fire Service told the Birmingham Mail the cause of the fire is being investigated, but did not rule out A-level students potentially having been the cause.

Horrifying aerial footage shows the blaze ripping through a 40-acre residential area, destroying homes and gardens.



Around six properties have reportedly been impacted so far, with drone footage showing homes completely gutted and covered in ash.

A rescue centre has been set up for those forced to flee their homes.

Local resident Jane Baxter said she could see the flames from her “bedroom window” and described the “horrendous” choking smell in the air.

She and neighbours were given a few minutes to gather their belongings before fleeing, with the blaze just 200 yards away.

Stourbridge councillor Andrew Tromans said: “The apocalyptic scenes in Norton and across Stourbridge are sadly just a taste of what is to come if we don’t act.



“It is my view, and it has been for a while, that Dudley councillors must have an emergency meeting about [how] we protect our borough from the impacts of climate change.”

Cops are investigating the cause of the Stourbridge inferno, with reports of it starting in a nearby grassland before spreading to homes.

A large fire also broke out in neighbouring Pershore on Thursday afternoon, with Hereford and Worcester Fire Service treating one person for smoke inhalation.

A total of 11 major fire incidents were reported in the past 24 hours, according to the National Fire Chiefs Council chairman.

Phil Carrigan told the BBC’s Today programme: “It’s been a particularly difficult, busy period for the fire and rescue service, where we’ve been under significant pressure.



“Firefighters have been on the front line of climate change for a number of years. They’re doing their absolute best to protect communities and properties.”

The surge in fires came as the UK officially broke its 2026 record for the hottest day, with the mercury hitting 38.5C in Kew Gardens, London.

Paying tribute to firefighters on the ground, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: “Awful to see homes and communities hit by fires across the country tonight as the heatwave continues.

“Our firefighters are working in incredibly difficult conditions and putting themselves at risk to keep others safe.

“A huge thank you to them and everyone supporting the effort tonight.”



Six firefighters from the West Midlands service have been admitted to hospital since the outbreak, suffering from heat exhaustion and smoke inhalation.

Anthony Marsh, the chief executive of the West Midlands Ambulance Service, said: “Yesterday was an extremely busy day for our crews, responding to a number of serious fires across the region.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I want to thank all of our staff for their professionalism and hard work, as well as our colleagues in the fire and police services for the way everyone worked together to help keep people safe.

“With the hot and dry weather we have encountered, we would ask everyone to take extra care and think about the risks before lighting fires or undertaking activities that could cause them.”

News.title: M25 closed in BOTH directions as air ambulance lands on motorway after crash
News.content:
TRAVEL CHAOS M25 closed in BOTH directions as air ambulance lands on motorway after crash

A MAJOR motorway has been closed in both directions as an air ambulance lands on the road following a serious crash.

The M25 in Leatherhead, Surrey has shut between J9 and J10.

The carriageway has been temporarily closed on both sides of J9 and the slip road to allow the air ambulance to land.

The injured motorist has been rushed to hospital as traffic continues to build up.





It’s not yet clear when the carriageway will reopen.

National Highways has reported delays of nearly 80 minutes following the incident.

Traffic cameras are showing lengthy queues and stationary motorists on the M25 clockwise near Leatherhead.

Surrey Police have told drivers to use alternative routes for the time being or factor in this potential delay into your journey.

The force said: “There are road closures in place on the M25 following a collision on the anticlockwise carriageway of the M25 just past J9.

“The carriageway was temporarily closed on both sides on the junction and slip road to allow the air ambulance to land.

“The injured party has been taken to hospital by road and we expect the air ambulance to be lifting before too long and the carriageways to reopen imminently, but please use alternative routes for the time being or factor in this potential delay into your journey.”

News.title: Massive fire erupts at ‘migrant hotel’ yards from Wembley Stadium as footage shows raging inferno & smoke billowing
News.content:
A MASSIVE inferno has broken out at a hotel, believed to be housing migrants, just yards away from Wembley Stadium.

The London Fire Brigade received the first of 29 calls reporting the blaze at the alleged migrant hotel at around 12.30 this afternoon.



Crews rushed to the Holiday Inn, on Empire Way, Wembley and managed to bring the blaze under control around an hour after arriving.

Six fire engines and around 40 firefighters were scrambled to fight the flames.



The Home Office said that it could not comment on the use of the hotel as migrant accommodation.

Closed to guests, the Holiday Inn was being used as asylum seeker accommodation in August last year.



Images and video captured by shocked bystanders show a thick plume of black smoke rising into the air above the migrant hotel.

Firefighters were seen administering first aid to evacuated hotel guests, holding oxygen masks up to their mouths.



Further images show what appear to be members of the public assisting fire crews with hydrants in the street as they scramble to get water on the burning building.

Crews can be seen using ladders to douse the flames in water as the fire burns behind them.

Images of the aftermath of the fire show exterior walls of the building blackened and charred by the heat of the blaze.

It remains unclear what sparked the inferno at this time.

The London Fire Brigade (LFB) said it had launched an investigation into the cause of the fire.



LFB said: “Six fire engines and around 40 firefighters responded to a fire at a hotel on Empire Way, Wembley.

“The Brigade received the first of 29 calls reporting the fire at 1234.

“Control officers mobilised crews from Park Royal, Willesden, Northolt and surrounding fire stations to the scene.

“Firefighters were able to bring the fire under control by 1321.

“The cause of the fire is under investigation.”

News.title: Is it right to ban disposable barbecues? VOTE NOW
News.content:
POLL OF THE DAY Is it right to ban disposable barbecues? VOTE NOW

ANDY Burnham has temporarily banned disposable barbeques in the wake of wildfires ripping through the UK.

The ban is coming into force because the single use BBQs “have been the cause of a number of serious wildfires across the country over the summer months”.

Retailers and distributors have been warned against selling the products, with potential “criminal sanctions” for those who don’t comply.

A government statement added: “Disposable barbecues cannot be considered a safe product in the context of the ongoing weather and environmental conditions and must not be made available for sale either in store or online at the current time.”





The PM warned the public not to light an open fire of “any kind” and to dispose of cigarettes carefully.

News.title: Afghan men ‘laughed as they filmed gang-rape of unconscious teen, 17’ as one of three suspects, 25, arrested in London
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

CHILLING 'ATTACK' Afghan men ‘laughed as they filmed gang-rape of unconscious teen, 17’ as one of three suspects, 25, arrested in London

THREE Afghan men allegedly laughed as they gang-raped an unconscious 17-year-old girl, filming the entire attack on their phones.

Quais W, 20, Kambiz H, 25, and Burhanulla N, 19, are on trial in Dortmund, Germany.



Kambiz, a window cleaner, was arrested in London after allegedly fleeing the scene of the crime.

The three men are accused of approaching the young girl at a bus stop at 4am on September 2024.



They allegedly took the teen back to their flat, where they plied her with booze.

Then when she fell unconscious, the men attacked, prosecutors said.

Public prosecutor Fabian Weishaupt told Bild: “During the night, the witness lost consciousness as a result of alcohol consumption.

“The defendants then took advantage of this condition.”

The men are charged with sexual assault, bodily harm and producing child pornography.

A horror video filmed on one of the alleged rapists’ phones showed all three of the men laughing, cops said.



Police said the trio repeatedly abused the defenceless girl.

All three defendants were already known to police, Bild reported.

Quais is reportedly known to cops for drug offenses, robbery, and assaulting law enforcement officers.

Burhanulla is known for drug trafficking and robbery, Bild reported.

Kambiz has reportedly been linked to assault and threats.



The men remained silent in court and are considering whether to comment on the charges.

Cops will then show the video footage of the alleged offence.

On the third day of the trial, their alleged victim is set to take the stand.

News.title: Disposable barbecues are BANNED over ‘significant fire risk’ after spate of monster blazes across the UK
News.content:
DISPOSABLE barbeques have been temporarily banned due to the “signficant risk” of fires.

The Government order was made after “apocalyptic” blazes broke out across the West Midlands and fires raged in parts of the UK.



Retailers and distributors have been warned against selling the products, with potential “criminal sanctions” for those who don’t comply.

On a visit to the scene of the devastating blazes in Prime Minister Andy Burnham described the country as a “tinderbox”.



And he urged the public to take the “greatest of care” and “don’t light anything in an outdoor space right now” – also warning cigarette smokers about danger.

Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live, he said: “All retailers will be receiving guidance today, asking them to withdraw them from sale.



“We’ve got 37 fires across England and Wales right now, four of them are major incidents.

“I can’t on this call today say to you that all of them are down to disposable barbecues, they’re not, and I wouldn’t, wouldn’t claim that.



“But it’s probable that some of them have been caused in that in that way.”

The new guidance, issued today by the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade, states: “Disposable barbecues have been the cause of a number of serious wildfires across the country over the summer months.

“During the current drought and heatwave conditions, the government considers that the supply and subsequent foreseeable use of disposable barbecues poses a significant risk to the public, and the environment, and therefore cannot be considered a safe product.

“They should not be made available for supply either in store or online at the current time.

“These guidelines will be kept under review, and will be withdrawn in consultation with relevant departments and agencies, as weather conditions change sufficiently to significantly reduce the risks.”



Burnham had suggested earlier in the week that such a measure could be introduced.

Speaking in Stourbridge, he told reporters: “Britain is a tinderbox right now, and please just have that in your mind.

“We’re going to go into the rest of the weekend… This is not over by any means.”

He went on to say the Government will commission firefighting planes to combat the spread of wildfires – as used to douse flames in Europe and the US, to combat the spread of wildfires..

The PM added an “emergency support” package is being drawn up for fire services battling the blazes.



Where are the fires raging? AS temperatures soar, several huge wildfires are ravaging the UK, many consuming entire homes, cars and forests. Several blazes are burning in the West Midlands, including in: Stourbridge

Around a hundred firefighters are tackling a massive, out-of-control grass and woodland fire on Racecourse Lane, right by the Stourbridge golf course. Multiple homes have caught fire. Salford Priors, Stratford-upon-Avon Another major incident has been declared as a blaze rages in Warwickshire. Druids Heath

Fire looks like it has broken out on land near Manningford Road and Pennyacre Road in the Druids Heath area of Birmingham. Solihull

A localised outdoor blaze has broken out, drawing responsive fire apparatus to contain it before it spreads to adjacent hedges. In other parts of England, fires rage in: Rainham

A car fire spread rapidly into the roadside grass fencing. The incident has caused traffic chaos, with Ferry Lane being closed both ways. Mousehold Heath, Norwich A major fire in woodland has sent plumes of smoke over Norwich and shut down roads in the city. And seven major wildfires are burning in South Wales, with hotspots including: Porth (Rhondda) A new fire is raging heavily next to residential properties, forcing crews to aggressively drench homes. Blaenavon (Cwmavon Woods) A massive hill and woodland blaze has been burning for days. Fires are also actively spreading through Merthyr Tydfil, Rudry Forestry, Mountain Ash (Cefn Pennar), and Newport.

He said: “Firstly, we have seen the military deploy 100 personnel, initially to the major incident in South Wales, and we’re very grateful to our colleagues in the Ministry of Defence for that. That support is critically needed.

“We have a system of mutual aid in play at the moment, where fire and rescue services are supporting each other, but with so many incidents, it is crucial that the military support is there if fire and rescue services can’t do the same backup that they would normally be doing.

“So that is hugely appreciated.

“The second issue is around aerial firefighting capability, the planes that people might see in other countries.



“We have taken a decision to deploy nationally aerial firefighting support, so commissioned nationally.

“But that obviously wasn’t available here, but it will be available elsewhere, and it would have made a difference.”

Earlier today he praised firefighters working in “incredibly difficult conditions” in Stourbridge, as well as other blazes across the West Midlands and the UK fuelled by extreme heat and high winds.

Six firefighters are among 25 people in hospital following the wildfires, beginning on Thursday afternoon – with families describing seeing ash “raining from the sky” as they grabbed their bags and fled.



Mr Burnham wrote on X: “Awful to see homes and communities hit by fires across the country tonight as the heatwave continues.

“My thoughts are with everyone affected, particularly those who have been injured or forced from their homes, and with the firefighters who have been taken to hospital.”

The PM also said he will be “speaking to emergency service on the ground”, as he paid tribute to the firefighters working through “incredibly difficult conditions” to bring the wildfires under control.

He thanked emergency services, adding: “Our firefighters are working in incredibly difficult conditions and putting themselves at risk to keep others safe.”



Chair of the National Fire Chiefs Council (NFCC) Phil Garrigan told BBC Radio 4’s Today Programme: “It’s not just the Stourbridge incident that we’ve dealt with over the last 24 hours.

“We’ve had 11 major incidents declared across the UK – Stourbridge particularly, but Sandwell, Pershore, Stoke-on-Trent. We’ve got incidents still raging in Hampshire, in South Wales.

“It’s been a particularly difficult, busy period for the fire and rescue service, where we’ve been under significant pressure.

“Firefighters have been on the front line of climate change for a number of years. They’re doing their absolute best to protect communities and properties.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Asked whether people were being encouraged on social media to start fires, Mr Garrigan said: “If people are encouraged to, and when people take those kind of directions and start fires, and those fires have an impact that they’ve had in West Midlands – then the individuals who have caused those fires will find themselves behind bars.



“I would be certainly discouraging them from taking any action and following any direction from anyone online, or anyone else for that matter.”

News.title: Temporary ban on sale of disposable BBQs over wildfire risk
News.content:
Disposable barbecues "cannot be considered a safe product" in the current conditions and they "must not be made available for sale either in store or online at the current time" in Great Britain, advice published by DBIST said, external.

All retailers will be receiving guidance about the change, which will be kept under review, Burnham told the BBC.

Burnham also said some of the wildfires burning across the country will have been started by disposable barbecues.

Speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live's Matt Chorley, the prime minister said: "We've got 37 fires across England and Wales right now, four of them are major incidents."

He added: "We're going into a difficult weekend, please just think about the situation that we're in.

"Britain is a tinderbox right now. Setting a fire in any outdoor setting of any kind is a risk to other people's homes, it's a risk to other people's lives, don't do it, please don't do it."

Many large retailers and supermarkets had already voluntarily stopped selling the devices under a framework agreed in 2023 between fire chiefs and the British Retail Consortium.

It said that retailers should suspend sales once an extreme heat event has been declared as imminent, or in response to "reasonable, evidence based" requests from local councils.

News.title: Farage faces renewed watchdog probe after Clacton by-election victory
News.content:
A parliamentary standards investigation into a Â£5m gift received by Nigel Farage has been reopened following the Reform UK leader's by-election win in Clacton.

The investigation into an alleged failure to declare an interest was paused after Farage resigned as an MP last month in response to scrutiny of his financial backing, triggering the by-election.

Farage won with 63% of the vote on a turnout of 44% in a highly unusual by-election that was contested by a record 34 candidates but was boycotted by all of the main Westminster parties.

Farage did not show up at the count, telling supporters Essex Police had warned him of an "organised campaign to disrupt and degrade the result".

The BBC has been told Essex Police did not advise any candidate that they should not attend the count.

Speaking to supporters before the result was announced, Farage said: "I'm damned if I'm going to stand on a stage, having won a resounding victory, a ringing endorsement of all that I've tried to fight for, and you've tried to fight for, and be demeaned and humiliated by nobodies, and I will not sadly be attending the count."

Reform UK cancelled what the party had billed as a "major speech" by Farage in Clacton on Friday morning and some scheduled media appearances.

In a statement, the Reform leader said: "The verdict is now in, and it is a convincing, overwhelming win, with more votes than we got in the general election of 2024.

"Today, the voters in Clacton have stuck up two fingers to the entire political establishment."

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he recognised that voters in the area had "come up with their answer" but that the investigation should continue.

"It needs to be resolved to make sure we've got the highest standards in politics, and that's incumbent on all of us, including Mr Farage," he told BBC Radio 5 Live.

Farage received 22,239 votes, 1,014 more than his winning total at the general election in 2024, when he first became the MP for Clacton, and increased his majority from 8,405 to 12,784.

The turnout was about 14% lower than it was in the 2024 general election in the constituency but about average for recent Westminster by-elections.

News.title: Prisoners charged over attack on Sara Sharif's father
News.content:
Two prisoners have been charged with the attempted murder of fellow inmate Urfan Sharif who was jailed for killing his daughter Sara Sharif.

Steven Sansom, 47, and Adam Watson, 39, have also been charged with other offences relating to the incident in Belmarsh Prison on 1 January 2025, the Crown Prosecution Service said.

The men will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court for a first hearing on 26 August.

Sharif, 43, and Sara's stepmother Beinash Batool were sentenced to life imprisonment after being convicted at the Old Bailey for murdering 10-year-old Sara at their home in Woking, Surrey.

Sharif reportedly suffered cuts to his face during the attack, and received medical treatment at the prison.

Daren Streeter, deputy chief crown prosecutor at CPS London, said: "Our prosecutors have worked closely with the Metropolitan Police to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring the case to court and pursue criminal proceedings."

Sara was hooded, burned and beaten during a "campaign of torture" that lasted two years before her body was found at the family home in August 2023.

During the trial, Justice Cavanagh told the court "the degree of cruelty involved is almost inconceivable".

Urfan Sharif was sentenced to a minimum of 40 years in prison for murder, while his wife Beinash Batool, 30, received a minimum of 33 years.

Sara's uncle, Faisal Malik, 29, was sentenced to 16 years' imprisonment for causing or allowing her death.

The three fled to Islamabad, Pakistan, with Sara's five siblings, the day before her body was found, prompting an international manhunt.

They hid out there for four weeks before returning to the UK, where they were arrested.

News.title: Eurovision proposes new rules to reduce political voting
News.content:
Organisers of the Eurovision Song Contest are proposing major rule changes to discourage voting campaigns that aim to influence the results.

Under the current system, viewers can vote up to 10 times for their favourite act by phone, text message or online.

In a letter to participating broadcasters, the EBU reportedly suggested moving the vote entirely online and forcing the public to select their top three acts - instead of being able to vote multiple times for one contestant.

The EBU said politically motivated voting had become "persistent" and was seen by many as "deeply worrying". The voting rules have been under scrutiny since the Israeli government encouraged fans to register multiple votes for the country's contestant in 2025.

Yuval Raphael's song, New Day Will Rise, placed 15th with the contest's juries - but outperformed every other participant in the public vote, scoring 297 points. In the end, Raphael finished as the overall runner-up.

A number of broadcasters subsequently queried how Israel placed so highly. They pointed to the fact that official social media accounts linked to Israel's government, including that of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, had asked people to vote for Raphael 20 times, the maximum allowed.

News.title: 'Glam helps mentality' says sprinter Amy Hunt, but can it give you that winning edge?
News.content:
They say practice makes perfect, but for some athletes that means more than just training to be as fast as possible.

For many, it's also about what you wear or how you accessorise with things like jewellery.

So can getting glammed up help your performance?

British sprinter Amy Hunt certainly thinks so, and it seems to be working as she's now secured two gold medals at the European Athletics Championships.

The 24-year-old, who's gunning for a historic quadruple win at the event this week, told BBC Newsbeat "the glam definitely helps that mentality because sprinting is such a confidence game".

"Everyone knows I love a bit of glam and I love my nails."

The Midlands-born athlete has curated her nail art to reference landmarks within Birmingham, where the competition is being held, including nods to the Jewellery Quarter and the Bull Ring, external.

Hunt says "looking good and feeling good" is all part of her process to get into the right mindset, and likens walking out on to the track to a gladiator entering an arena.

"It's a show at the end of the day," she says.

Fellow athletes, including Olympic champions Keely Hodgkinson and the United States' Sha'Carri Richardson and Noah Lyles, are among those who have also become known for their statement nail art on the field, but it's by no means a new practice.

US Olympic champion track star Florence Griffith Joyner, known as Flo-Jo, is often regarded as a pioneer of competing with long, vibrant nails back in the 1980s.

News.title: You got hold of eclipse glasses just in time - here's what to do with them now
News.content:
Millions of us were treated to a stunning spectacle on Wednesday during mainland Europe's first total solar eclipse for more than 25 years.

And for some in the UK, it was a race against time to find a pair of eye-protecting eclipse glasses as shortages grew.

If you did manage to grab some, you might be asking - what do I do with them now?

"Eclipse glasses are a great example of our single-use culture," says Dr Renee Tonkin, the founder of Science Owl, an environmental education organisation focused on waste.

"Particularly because they're difficult to recycle due to their mixed materials."

According to Recycle Now, which advises on appropriate places to recycle items, the glasses are not wholly recyclable in your household waste.

It says you can recycle the cardboard frames so long as you separate them from the lenses, which are harder to recycle.

So here are three things you can do with those retina-saving spectacles.

News.title: What we know so far about the West Midlands fires
News.content:
Harrowing stories have emerged from people who had their homes destroyed by fire.

Andrew Reynolds, whose mother's house burnt down in Highters Heath area of Birmingham, said his family had lost everything, including 100 years' worth of family photos.

He described the scene as an "inferno" as the blaze "ripped through" the properties.

Reynolds, 42, said: "Everyone's gutted, grieving, people have lost so much and no-one can go in to see if they can salvage anything."

Jane Baxter, whose house backs directly on Stourbridge Golf Club, was evacuated from her home.

She told BBC Radio 4's Today programme: "The police knocked our door and said that everyone had to be evacuated quickly because they thought the fire was changing directions.

"So, it was literally grab what you need and get out.

"So, get out we did with the cat and away to go to our son's house."

Farmers in the area tried to use tractors to make a firebreak to halt the spread of the blaze.

Daniel Pardoe, of Iverley Park Farm, said: "There was about eight of us in total with various tractors and sprayers."

A total of 54 people were treated by paramedics, with 19 admitted to hospital, following the fires, West Midlands Ambulance Service said.

News.title: I got an £89 refund – how to cancel and  avoid unwanted subscriptions
News.content:
Ever been confused by a random amount leaving your bank then had that sinking feeling it's a subscription you forgot to cancel or didn't mean to sign up to?

From TV streaming, to meal deliveries and beauty boxes there are subscriptions for almost everything.

Often the first order is free or heavily discounted so you give it a try and tell yourself you'll cancel it before the deadline. But it's easy to forget and sometimes not straightforward.

Following Prime Minister Andy Burnham's crackdown on subscription traps, three people tell us how they got into - and out of theirs.

News.title: Mother jailed for killing baby by burning her with a hairdryer
News.content:
A mother who killed her baby daughter by burning her with a hairdryer has been jailed for six years.

Courtney Gartshore, 28, used the appliance to subject three-month-old Dahlia-Rose to "significant and sustained heat" on her head and body.

Emergency services were called to the scene at a property in Peterhead, Aberdeenshire, in September 2023, but the child had died.

Gartshore was convicted of culpable homicide - the closest equivalent to manslaughter in Scots Law - following a trial at the High Court in Aberdeen in July.

Warning: This article contains details readers may find upsetting

Sentencing Gartshore at the High Court in Edinburgh, judge Simon Collins KC told her, external she had inflicted "severe and disfiguring" burns on her daughter.

He said: "Given Dahlia-Rose's very young age, and the horrifying way that she died, this is a uniquely disturbing and distressing case.

"But it is tragic as well as terrible. And that is because the evidence suggested that the accused loved Dahlia-Rose, yet will have to live the rest of her life with the knowledge that she was responsible for her death."

News.title: Sign of life as bright orange 'fire fungus' grows at park ravaged by wildfire
News.content:
A fungus that grows in places damaged by fire has been found at the site of a major wildfire in the Cairngorms National Park.

Forestry and Land Scotland (FLS) said the bright orange, pyrophilous (fire-loving) fungus could be the first sign of nature's recovery at Glenmore near Aviemore.

A wildfire started in the area on 15 July and the incident, which has burned through thousands of acres of woodland and moor, continues to be monitored for hotspots.

FLS said the fungus was among the "first colonisers" of burned ground and played a role in breaking down carbon and preventing soil erosion.

News.title: One million sign petition to keep PC Harper's killers in jail
News.content:
A petition to block the early release of PC Andrew Harper's killers has been signed by more than one million people.

The police officer, from Wallingford, Oxfordshire, died in 2019 when he was dragged by a car as three teenagers fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Berkshire.

Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers were sentenced to 13 years for his manslaughter in 2020 but could be released next year under plans to tackle prison overcrowding. The prime minister is looking at ways to keep them in jail.

Thames Valley Police (TVP) Federation acknowledged the important milestone the petition had reached "without fanfare" due to the seventh anniversary of the officer's death on Saturday.

The petition was started by TVP federation chair Aileen O'Connor who said the decision to consider the killers for early release "pours salt into wounds that have never healed".

She added it was an "insult to Andrew's family, his friends, his colleagues and the entire policing family".

The federation thanked all those who have signed in support.

News.title: Disability campaigners call for Burnham to delay assisted dying bill
News.content:
Disabled and terminally ill campaigners have written to Prime Minister Andy Burnham urging him to reform social and palliative care before assisted dying legislation is introduced in England and Wales.

The Assist Us To Live group says people are currently being "failed by society" and "introducing assisted dying in these circumstances will put sick and disabled people's lives at risk".

Burnham believes the funding of palliative and social care should be "fixed" before assisted dying is considered. The government is likely to remain officially neutral, but the PM's remarks suggest he personally will not back the bill proposed by Labour MP Lauren Edwards.

Bill supporters argue improving care services and giving terminally ill people "autonomy" over their final weeks must go hand in hand.

The proposed law - known as the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill - would allow people over the age of 18 who were expected to die within six months to be given help to end their own life, subject to certain safeguards.

Having a disability in and of itself does not mean you would be able to seek help to end your life.

This is the second time a backbench bill like this is going through the House of Commons.

MPs voted in favour of a bill proposed by Labour MP Kim Leadbetter in 2025, but it was not passed by the House of Lords after an unprecedented number of suggested amendments delayed its progress until it ran out of time in April this year.

Edwards reintroduced an identical bill in June in order to "finish the job" started by Leadbeater. It is due to be debated in the Commons on 11 September.

Opponents of the bill believe the legislation has substantial flaws and would pose risks to disabled people, putting pressure on them to end their lives.

The Equality and Human Rights Commission, the UK's regulator, says legislation is "likely to have particular impacts on people with certain protected characteristics, especially older and disabled people, external".

Last year, the commission's chair Baroness Falkner said: "While the bill provides safeguards against a person being coerced or pressured to end their own life by another individual, we know that disabled people, older people and especially older disabled people, may feel pressured to prematurely end their lives by societal attitudes and a lack of the support and services they need."

Edwards has said there is time to improve end-of-life care before any assisted dying service would come into effect under her proposed law, given a four-year implementation period had been agreed in the previous debates.

News.title: NHS service admits data breach due to pager use
News.content:
The sensitive medical data of transplant patients from across the UK was routinely sent over an unencrypted pager network, an NHS service has admitted.

A BBC investigation found NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) sent the names, dates of birth and types of organs being offered or needed to members of hospital transplant teams who were using pagers, unaware they were not encrypted.

In 2019, then-Health Secretary Matt Hancock announced the NHS in England should stop using pagers by 2021, but some parts of the organisation have continued doing so.

NHSBT said it was "deeply sorry" and has reported the data breach to the Information Commissioner. It added it has now stopped sending patient data in this way.

Pagers are small battery operated radio receivers - popular in the 1980s and 1990s - that can receive short text messages, numbers to call, or alerts.

They are a one-way communication system and only able to receive messages, not send them, which was why they largely fell out of public use as more and more people started carrying mobile phones.

News.title: Man died after being 'trampled' by cattle on estate
News.content:
A man injured in the grounds of a National Trust estate died from "severe chest injuries" after being trampled by cattle, an inquest has heard.

John Orton, 78, a retired telecommunications engineer, died at Felbrigg Hall, near Cromer in Norfolk on 13 July.

Assistant coroner for Norfolk, Maeve Sykes, opened an inquest into his death at Norfolk Coroner's Court on Friday and said a post-mortem examination gave a provisional cause of death as "severe chest injuries".

A National Trust spokesperson said: "We have been left shocked and deeply saddened by the death of a visitor who was seriously injured while walking at Felbrigg last month."

On 13 July, Norfolk Police were called to the estate at about 11:45 BST and said despite efforts to save him, Orton died at the scene.

Following the incident, the estate was closed while inquiries were carried out.

News.title: Final day of heatwave for many before weekend cooldown
News.content:
Kew Gardens in London reached 38.1C on Thursday, making it the UK's hottest day of 2026 so far, and the fifth hottest UK day on record.

It is also the second time this year that the temperature has reached 38C, after Lingwood, Norfolk recorded 38.0C on 26 June.

This is only the second time that 38C has been reached twice in the same year - the previous occasion being 2022.

Though the Met Office amber warning for extreme heat that covered large swathes of England on Thursday expired at midnight, high temperatures will linger in central and eastern parts of England on Friday.

Long spells of sunshine will lift temperatures to 29-34C (84-93F) across large parts of the Midlands, Lincolnshire, East Anglia and the south-east.

For many places it will mark a third consecutive day above official heatwave thresholds.

The heat will ease elsewhere.

Somewhat cooler conditions will begin to move into northern and western parts of the UK, although temperatures will generally remain above the norm for the time of year - widely reaching the low to mid-20s Celsius.

Many places will be dry with a mix of cloud and sunny spells although a few showers are possible, and these could be heavy and thundery in some places.

News.title: Brothers injured by 'exploding' steam room door
News.content:
Two children from Harrogate were hurt after a steam room door shattered while they were in Turkey on a package holiday.

The brothers, who were 11 and 16 at the time of the incident, were staying at the Green Nature Diamond Hotel with their parents. CCTV footage sourced from the hotel by their father shows the moment the glass door shattered, leaving them with cuts to various parts of their bodies.

Jet2Holidays initially denied liability, but later agreed to pay Â£7,000 compensation to the family.

The travel company said: "We would like to reiterate how sorry we are about this incident."

Legal proceedings are underway in three separate cases of sexual assault, including against two girls, in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta – amid warnings that 4,000 migrant children could be outside the protection system.

Both the alleged perpetrators and the survivors are believed to be migrants who crossed the border into Ceuta during the mass arrival of up to 80,000 people two weeks ago.

Two of the suspects, accused of touching a minor and of raping a minor, with an additional allegation of drug trafficking, are in custody.

Another, accused of touching an adult woman, is due to be deported to Morocco, the High Court of Justice of Andalusia said.

It comes amid concern for thousands of migrant children that remain homeless and outside the protection system. Some are as young as 9, according to Save the Children.

While the majority of the migrants who crossed into the Spanish territory were returned to Morocco, according to Spain, most unaccompanied minors either cannot be returned as they are protected by child welfare laws.

While around 1,500 children and adolescents are within the protection system, an estimated 4,000 are not. Some are waiting to be identified and referred, but others are sleeping on the streets, exposed to violence, exploitation and trafficking, aid organisations warned.

Images of children sleeping rough on Ceuta's streets, and reports of parents searching for missing children, have caused outrage. Meanwhile, Moroccan media reported that calls for a fresh mass crossing on Saturday have been circulating on social media, raising fears of a worsening crisis.

At least 100 people were killed during the last mass crossing, according to Ceuta’s leader.

The Moroccan Interior Ministry said on Thursday that security monitoring had been reinforced in areas close to both crossings, while Spanish authorities warned that the border remained closed.

Save the Children told The Independent it is “extremely concerned about the risk of sexual violence, exploitation and trafficking” of unaccompanied children.

As well as a lack of access to sufficient food and safe shelter, there is a lack of adequate hygiene and healthcare. Girls have reported urinary infections, StC said. For those in emergency shelters in local warehouses, food may be limited to one meal a day.

“The situation remains extremely concerning,” said Raúl Arnaiz, director of Spanish programmes for StC, who is currently in Ceuta. “[Our] team on the ground has observed significant gaps in access to food, hygiene products and adequate sanitation.”

Many of the children who arrived at the enclave have taken complex journeys to get there, sometimes through multiple countries and from countries affected by conflict and serious humanitarian crises.

Omar, whose name has been changed to protect his identity, a teenager from Sudan, is now living on a beach in Ceuta. He travelled for a year and half, through Algeria, Libya, Chad and Morocco, before arriving at the enclave.

The minors may eventually be transferred to Spain, however.

"I think it might only be a matter of a few weeks before we start seeing (minors) transferred to and welcomed on the mainland,” Youth Minister Sira Rego has said.

“The situation in Ceuta is tragic,” the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement said, adding that they are deploying additional personnel to Andalusia due to the high number of people requiring assistance.

White House border czar Tom Homan defended a new tool that Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers could soon add to their arsenal: electric shock gloves.

In a Thursday interview with Fox News, Homan was asked about the device, known by the acronym GLOVE — short for Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter.

“How would that work and what role would they play?” host Brian Kilmeade asked.

“Well look, it’s another device to help someone be compliant when they’re not,” Homan responded. He cast the gloves as an alternative to lethal force, arguing, “you just can't go from 0 to 100.”

The gloves, Homan said, could be deployed in detention facilities during fights and in situations “where detainees get out of control.” He also pointed to what he said had been a sharp rise in threats against federal agents.

open image in gallery White House Border Czar Tom Homan defended ICE's new electric gloves as an alternative to lethal force. The government plans to spend up to $20 million to equip agents with the gloves ( Getty )

Still, President Donald Trump’s border czar stressed that the devices are not poised for an immediate rollout, saying there are “still some training issues that need to be dealt with.”

The interview came three days after the Department of Homeland Security posted a notice saying ICE planned to spend up to $20 million on the devices for officers by March 2027.

The gloves — manufactured by Compliant Technologies LLC in Kentucky – have already been used by jails and certain police departments. When activated and applied to someone’s skin, they deliver a pain stimulus.

“The G.L.O.V.E. quickly transforms into a CD3 (Conductive Distraction and De-escalation Device) when used within the Force Continuum to supplement existing tools for law enforcement, corrections, security, EMS and the military,” Compliant Technologies’ website states. “It is available as an ‘invisible partner’ to enhance the user's effectiveness when operating within their agencies' already established tactics, techniques and procedures.”

open image in gallery 'It’s another device to help someone be compliant when they’re not,' Homan told Fox News. 'You know you just cant go from 0 to 100' ( Fox News )

Civil rights advocates expressed alarm at the news that federal agents could soon be equipped with the devices.

“ICE spent the last year showing this country they are too quick to use force,” Jenn Rolnick Borchetta, deputy project director at the American Civil Liberties Union, told The Associated Press.

“Now they will be able to deploy electric shocks with the slight push of a button that maybe nobody else can see them do,” she added. “Introducing gloves that can so easily be used to deliver terrible pain in encounters is a recipe for harm to the public.”

The tactics of federal immigration agents have come under intense scrutiny over the past year amid Trump’s immigration crackdown.

In a Marist poll conducted one month after the fatal shootings of two U.S. citizens in Minnesota, nearly two-thirds of Americans said ICE’s actions had gone too far.

DHS’ independent watchdog has opened multiple investigations into the department, including over ICE’s hiring program, use of force and detention facilities.

Media mogul Alex Cooper is reportedly shutting down her drinks brand, Unwell Beverages, nearly two years after launching the hydration product aimed at women.

Cooper’s company will release new Halloween-themed drinks later this year before ceasing “production across all of the brand’s line of beverages,” according to a Bloomberg report that cited sources close to the situation.

The Call Her Daddy host and Nestlé launched Unwell Beverages and its first electrolyte-focused line, Unwell Hydration, in early 2025. The range was expanded to different performance-focused drinks, including Unwell Focus, Unwell Protein and Unwell Energy.

Bloomberg reports that Target, Unwell’s main distributor, is selling through its stock. The Independent has contacted Cooper’s representatives, Nestlé and Target for comment.

Cooper had previously said she was inspired to launch the beverages arm of her business because she noticed that performance and hydration drinks were often catered to men.

open image in gallery Alex Cooper is reportedly shuttering the beverages arm of her business ( Getty Images for SiriusXM )

Earlier this week, Unwell announced a strategic investment from the firm WTSL, valuing the business at $500 million.

In a statement about the investment, Cooper said the company is “scaling on all fronts, combining nimbleness, social-first premium content, and our understanding of culture to serve this highly influential audience.

“With WTSL’s backing, the company is now also poised to accelerate our media platform’s growth through acquisitions and investments,” she said.

In June, the podcaster spoke out for the first time regarding toxic workplace claims at Unwell, urging people not to believe what they read on the internet.

The 31-year-old had been embroiled in allegations of a toxic work environment after a Vanity Fair report cited sources who alleged that Matt Kaplan — Cooper’s husband and business partner — was contributing to a toxic workplace.

The report detailed allegations from 40 unnamed sources who were current and former Unwell employees, who accused Kaplan of yelling and making inappropriate comments at staffers, which led some junior employees to have panic attacks and anxiety.

In the report, a representative for the couple called the allegations “false and outrageous claims” amounting to a “meritless hit piece.”

Speaking about the claims, Cooper told The Wall Street Journal in June: “I will say that building a startup, there is so much growth that comes with that, and I am extremely proud of what we have built at Unwell.”

open image in gallery Cooper and her husband Matt Kaplan, a film and TV producer, co-founded their parent company Trending Media in 2023 ( Getty )

open image in gallery Cooper launched Unwell Beverages in early 2025 ( Getty )

“And I will just kind of leave it at ‘don’t believe everything that you read on the internet’ — but I think everyone knows that at this point.”

Pressed further about the claims made by former or current employees, she said: “I think that we have done a really incredible job at Unwell, and I think if you walk the halls, there are so many people that are so happy to work at this company.”

The podcaster added that being a woman in her industry is “extremely difficult because you’re held to a complete different standard.”

She continued: “Whether it’s a smear campaign being created for someone’s narrative — whatever it be.”

Cooper and Kaplan, a film and TV producer, co-founded their parent company Trending Media in 2023.

Beyond podcasting and beverages, the company has produced a string of TV and film releases, including the Hannah Montana 20th Anniversary Special on Disney +, the Hulu reality series Love Overboard and the new Netflix dating show Let’s Marry Harry, starring Cooper’s friend Harry Jowsey.

Cooper rose to fame after founding the celebrity interview podcast Call Her Daddy in 2018. It has become one of the most-listened-to podcasts of all time, featuring celebrity guests including Kamala Harris, Kim Kardashian and Gwyneth Paltrow.

A Greater Anglia train has derailed near Wickford in Essex, the Independent understands.

Pictures on social media show a train that appears to have come off the tracks into the gravel but has remained upright.

It comes less than 24 hours after another train derailed in East Sussex, with one passenger saying she thought she “was going to die”.

Rachel Heath said: “I just remember thinking to myself that I was going to die. There was about two seconds where I genuinely thought this was it.”

She added: “It’s just absolutely terrifying.”

An MP has said that concerns were raised over the “bumpier” train tracks just one week before the incident, which injuring 20 people.

An investigation is now underway after the incident, which left two people with serious injuries, and a further 18 people taken to hospital.

The probe will establish the “root cause” of the incident, which saw three carriageways leave the railway between Lewes and Haywards Heath.

National Rail have warned of significant disruption to the line on Friday, with all trains cancelled between the two stations and rail replacement buses in place.

News.title: 9 best action cameras for capturing your biggest adventures, tested by a tech expert
News.content:
Offering huge potential for mounting and use, this is the smallest of the action cameras I tested. It’s also the one that I would use to film with Pip, my labrador, as the nano adds little bulk or weight.

There are a few key features of this small camera that I really liked from the outset. The first is the modular design – this isn’t the first time DJI has gone down this route, and while the older DJI action 2 was innovative, it didn’t really capture the imagination of users at the time, so DJI reverted to the more tried-and-tested box-like design. The osmo nano is more user-friendly in both approach and aesthetic design, with a focus on those who just entering the action camera market.

The modular design means that the main camera module features built-in battery and memory (Alastair Jennings/The Independent)

Setup is incredibly simple and with the internal 128GB of memory, you can essentially very quickly charge, step outside and get going. The modular design means that the main camera module features built-in battery and memory, which will provide around 60-90 minutes, depending on the settings and outdoor temperature.

Again, the same mounting system is used as seen on the DJI osmo action 6 and DJI osmo 360 (both included in this roundup), so if you do delve into the ecosystem then all accessories are cross-compatible. The camera module on its own will connect into the familiar Mimo app, where you can adjust settings, download, edit and share footage.

The screen can be attached either way, so it can be seen from in front of or behind the camera (Alastair Jennings/The Independent)

If you want more control, this is when the larger screen module can be attached. This uses the magnetic clamp system to securely attach to the base of the camera and the contacts on top ensure a decent data connection between the two. A great feature here is that the screen can be attached either way, so it can be seen from in front of or behind the camera. In use, it all felt solid enough, and while not to the level of robustness of the more traditional action camera designs, it still felt like the modules would stand up to more than a knock or two.

Thanks to its small size and light weight, the nano will also likely go unnoticed by your pet, so if you do want to catch a pet's eye view of the world, this is a fun option (with the right mounts, of course). It's also extremely easy to use and can connect wirelessly to the DJI Mic 3.

Donald Trump’s administration is asking the Supreme Court for permission to build a massive ballroom to replace the demolished East Wing of the White House after a federal appeals court rejected the president’s attempts to construct the sprawling facility without approval from Congress.

Federal courts have allowed the president to continue construction on what officials have described as an expansive underground bunker while questioning the legality of the entire project after destroying the East Wing to make way for a 90,000 square foot facility that the administration argues is vital to national security and the president’s safety.

In a 2-to-1 ruling last week, the U.S. Court of Appeals in Washington, D.C. said the Constitution gives Congress — not the president — authority to make substantial changes to the White House. That decision upheld an exclamation point-filled injunction by District Judge Richard Leon, who called the president the “steward” of the White House but not “the owner!”

“If allowed to go into effect, the injunction would wrongfully install a single district judge as sole arbiter of what further construction is ‘strictly necessary’ to protect the safety of the President, his family, staff members, and visitors to the White House, including foreign dignitaries, and presidents and prime ministers of other countries,” U.S. Solicitor General D. John Sauer wrote to the high court on Friday.

The appeals court decision has yet to go into effect, allowing construction to continue while the Supreme Court decides what to do next. Justices must decide by August 21.

Donald Trump’s administration is asking the Supreme Court for permission to continue construction on his ballroom project after federal courts repeatedly stressed he cannot move forward without congressional approval ( Reuters )

Costs for the project have exploded from an initial $200 million estimate to $400 million — with some believing it could cost upwards of $600 million. While Trump has said private donations will pay for the ballroom itself, the administration transferred more than $300 million from the Secret Service budget to cover security upgrades to the White House this summer.

The Trump administration has revealed in court filings that the ballroom isn’t the primary purpose for the project. Instead, the government is building a sprawling underground bunker with military installations on the site.

Courts have not prevented the government from continuing work on the bunker. The plaintiff in the case, the National Trust for Historic Preservation, never objected to that part of the project.

In response, the administration has promoted plans for a “drone port” on the ballroom’s roof and highlighted the fortress-like plans for the massive building.

In court filings, the Department of Justice called the ballroom is “a knitted, unified, cohesive part of the East Wing Project, which is vital for National Security, and is being constructed to ensure that the President can perform his constitutional duties in a safe and heavily secured facility.”

Previously “top secret” plans include “heavy steel, drone-proof roof, missile-resistant and drone-proof columns, bullet, ballistic, and blast-proof glass, Military-grade venting for air conditioning and heating.”

There are also plans for “bomb shelters, a state of the art hospital and medical facilities, Top Secret military installations, structures, and equipment, protective partitioning, and other features,” lawyers wrote.

The ballroom’s rooftop will also be “hermetically sealed to prevent malign forces from contaminating the circulating air, thereby threatening the lives of those inside.”

Trump recently posted several images to his Truth Social account that appeared to be designs for a “drone port” on the ballroom’s roof.

The images depicted numerous military drones, armed soldiers and refueling trucks that turn the typically placid grounds of the White House into a major military installation.

“This great and very important military asset sits atop the heavily protected Ballroom at the White House. It provides National Security for Washington, D.C., and will protect future Presidents!!!” Trump wrote.

After last week’s appeals court decision, Trump raged against what he called a “politically motivated” and “totally wrong” ruling that “severely jeopardizes the lives and welfare of the people who work, and will be working, at the White House.”

In the administration’s appeal to the Supreme Court, Sauer wrote that Trump has been the target of several threats the president’s life — urgently requiring a White House shield to protect him.

Sauer also claimed that an alleged Iranian threat to the president while traveling on Air Force One — prompting a covert operation to switch planes, leaving Cabinet officials, staff and the press on a “decoy” plane — was the latest assassination attempt.

“Buckling” occurs when steel rails expand as they get hotter and can start to curve.

Thousands of miles of steel track make up the UK’s rail network, absorbing heat up to 20C hotter than the air temperature, said Network Rail.

It added that most of the network can operate when track temperatures reach up to 46C (roughly 30C air temperature) and rails have been recorded at temperatures as high as 51C.

As steel expands when it gets hot, rails lengthen, causing tension against their neighbouring pieces of track.

When this happens, trains are stopped for safety, as “if there is no room for the rail to expand, the rail can buckle and we need to close the line to fix it before trains can run again,” says Network Rail.

John Lawrence, chair of the Institution of Engineering and Technology Railway Technical Network, said: “Ambient temperature and solar gain combine to push temperatures very high at track level and in trackside equipment. Track buckles and dewirements are what really worry engineers – despite years of focus, investment and improvement, rails can still buckle in extreme heat.

“That brings derailment risks, and overhead lines can sag and catch on pantographs, halting train movements or forcing lengthy reroutes.”

He added that “hidden failures” resulting from heat stress include signalling control, power supplies, and trackside telecoms.

“Lineside fires, sparked by anything from discarded rubbish to passing trains, can cause further disruption,” said Lawrence.

According to Lawrence, rail operators can tackle overheating tracks by painting them white – something which can lower track temperatures by 5C – and lubricating rail joints to allow for expansion.

Several operators already use temperature sensors on the rails and thermal imaging drones and helicopters to spot overheating equipment and carry out repairs overnight.

According to Network Rail, hot weather can also affect overhead power lines and the ground on which the track sits.

Around 44 per cent of all passenger trains in the UK are powered by overhead lines, according to the Office for Rail and Road (a further 26 per cent of trains – mostly in the South East – get power from a live “third rail”). As mapped by data website Rail Maps, routes electrified by overhead power lines include the East and West Coast Main Lines and routes from London to Cardiff.

In hot weather, the overhead lines can expand and sag, which means temporary speed restrictions have to be imposed to reduce forces on the track, which can lead to delays and cancellations.
