World.title: Adeleke vows to probe killings in Osun
World.content:
Gov Ademola Adeleke of Osun State

By Shina Abubakar

Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke has vowed to set up an independent inquiry commission to probe the political killings in the state.

The governor, whose speech was delivered by the Commissioner for Information and Public Enlightenment, Kolapo Alimi, said the commission is to ensure that those culpable are brought to justice.

While consoling families that lost loved ones, he said no life is worth sacrificing for anybody’s ambition.

His words, “Every life lost is an Osun life. Politics should never cost anyone his or her life, irrespective of political affiliation.

“The government under my watch wishes to assure the people of Osun State that next week Monday, immediately after the election, an Independent Commission of Inquiry will be constituted to investigate all reported killings and acts of violence connected with this election period.

“The Commission will establish the circumstances surrounding these incidents and recommend appropriate actions to ensure that everyone responsible is brought to justice, regardless of political affiliation, position or influence.”

He added that his administration would put in place a support system to compensate those who lost family members.

“The Government will also put in place a framework to support and compensate the families of those who lost their lives. The memories of all victims will be appropriately honoured.

“The election will come and go, but we will remain one people. We owe the dead justice, their families compassion, and the people of Osun a peaceful future,” he added.

World.title: 102-year-old man dies after alleged assault at pub
World.content:
By Enitan Abdultawab

A 102-year-old great-grandfather has died in hospital days after he was allegedly assaulted at a pub in Cwmbran, South Wales.

Phillip Ormerod died this week following the incident at the Crow’s Nest pub on August 1.

His son, Robert Ormerod, described him as a well-known local character who regularly visited the pub two or three times a week.

Phillip, who lived alone in the Llanyrafon neighbourhood where he had raised his family, had dementia but continued to visit the pub, where he became a familiar face among locals.

“I suppose he became a pub character,” Robert said, adding that some younger customers would buy his father drinks when he visited.

Robert said his father had been diagnosed with dementia a couple of years ago, although the family believed he may have had it before then.

As his eyesight deteriorated, Robert and his brother helped him with household chores and bought his food.

“I used to visit him regularly, and then towards the end me and my brother used to keep the house clean as best we could, and buy his food because his eyesight had deteriorated,” he said.

Reflecting on his father’s death, Robert said the loss was difficult despite the challenges associated with his father’s age and dementia.

“I feel sad – even though he could be difficult because of his age and dementia, still, you get used to him being around,” he said.

“Even though I suppose he wouldn’t go on forever, he would’ve carried on I think for a bit.”

Phillip had worked as a design draughtsman before retiring. He continued living in Llanyrafon after his wife died about 40 years ago and was regularly visited by his two sons.

Emergency services were called to the Crow’s Nest at about 10:25pm on August 1 following a report of an assault.

A 56-year-old man from Llanelli was arrested on suspicion of section 20 assault and remains under investigation.

The circumstances surrounding the alleged assault and Phillip’s death remain under investigation.

World.title: BBNaija 11: Barry explains why he chose Goddessa over Neche
World.content:
By Mary Agbabiaka

Big Brother Naija Season 11 housemate, Barry, has explained why he chose to pursue Goddessa despite having a crush on fellow housemate Neche, saying Neche had made it clear that he was not her type.

Barry disclosed this on Thursday during a conversation with Goddessa, who questioned whether his feelings for her were genuine or mainly driven by sexual attraction.

Goddessa told Barry, “I feel like your feelings for me is more of a sexual attraction.”

Barry defended his feelings, asking, “You think I would spend my day staring at you if it was just that?”

When Goddessa reminded him that he liked two people, Barry admitted that he had a crush on Neche but said he was not pursuing her.

“I have a crush on Neche,” he said.

However, Barry explained, “But I am not pursuing the crush. She has a man outside and I am not her type of man.”

Goddessa remained unconvinced, insisting that Barry’s behaviour towards her suggested “sexual tension.”

The exchange highlights the growing romantic tension between Barry and Goddessa as they continue to navigate their relationship inside the Big Brother Naija house.

World.title: FG urges wealthy Nigerians, organisations to build fire stations
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The Federal Government has called on wealthy Nigerians, philanthropists, business leaders and corporate organisations to invest in establishing fire stations across the country, declaring that firefighting is the responsibility of everyone.

Controller General of the Federal Fire Service, Adeyemi Samuel Olumode, gave the charge at a One-Day National Stakeholders’ Summit on Fire Safety, held on Thursday in Abuja.

The Service also inducted 37 Public Relations Officers PROs drawn from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory FCT into the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations NIPR.

Adeyemi, who spoke under the theme “Building a Resilient Fire Service for the 21st Century,” said Nigeria needed a multiplicity of strategically located fire stations to bring emergency response closer to communities and reduce response time.

He cited the Offa Descendant Association Fire Station, Oyo Town Fire Station, Idanre Fire Station, Bonny Island Fire Station and Kugbo Fire Station as examples of what could be achieved when individuals, communities and organisations invested directly in the safety of their people, describing such gestures as an investment in lives and property rather than mere philanthropy.

The Controller General noted that the summit also marked exactly one year since he assumed office on 14 August 2025, an anniversary he said provided an opportunity to reflect on the Service’s achievements over the past year rather than a deliberate coincidence.

He listed some of these achievements to include the rehabilitation of 40 firefighting appliances, the supply of two modern firefighting appliances and over 2,000 pieces of personal protective equipment, as well as the training of more than 700 cadet officers in basic firefighting, who have since been deployed across commands.

Adeyemi said the Service had also strengthened specialised capacity through counter-terrorism training in collaboration with the Office of the National Security Adviser ONSA and the armed forces, alongside ongoing upgrades to the National Fire Academy, which he said would become the best in Africa for training firefighters once reopened.

On the induction of the PROs, the Controller General described the exercise as historic, being the first time officers from the 36 states and the FCT had been brought together for a coordinated and structured training programme toward professional recognition and certification.

“This is much more than issuing certificates. We are professionalising the way the Federal Fire Service communicates with Nigerians. Our PROs must understand strategic communication, crisis communication, media relations, stakeholder engagement, public education, reputation management and the challenges created by misinformation, particularly during emergencies,” he said.

He added that a fire incident is not only an operational occurrence but also a communication one, stressing that public trust remained central to the Service’s ability to protect lives and property.

Adeyemi commended the Tertiary Education Trust Fund TETFund for its collaboration on fire safety in tertiary institutions, as well as the Tony Elumelu Foundation for partnering with the Service on fire safety preparedness training for 7,740 ordinary Nigerians, with a target of reaching 10 persons in every local government area.

He also appreciated the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations and Rightangle PR for supporting the Service’s professional communication capacity, alongside government and private-sector partners and members of the media.

The Controller General called on the public to play its part during emergencies by giving fire appliances a clear path, keeping unnecessary crowds away, and sharing verified information with responders.

World.title: World Cup failure: ‘I’m not afraid of being sacked’ — Madugu
World.content:
Madugu

By Enitan Abdultawab

Super Falcons head coach Justin Madugu says he is not afraid of losing his job following Nigeria’s failure to qualify for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup.

Nigeria’s hopes of reaching the tournament were ended on Thursday after the Super Falcons suffered a 2-1 defeat to South Africa in the qualifying playoffs.

The result means Nigeria will miss the Women’s World Cup for the first time since the tournament began in 1991.

Speaking to the press after the defeat, Madugu apologised to Nigerians and accepted responsibility for the team’s failure.

“First of all, I have to apologise to Nigerians over our inability to make it to the World Cup. It was not our intention. We came and did the best that we could, but our best was not good enough,” he said.

“We are very sorry for that, and we take full responsibility for everything that happened,” Madugu added.

The coach was also asked about calls for his dismissal following the disappointing result.

“I am not afraid of being sacked. To the glory of God, I have served my country. It was a privilege that was given to me,” Madugu said.

He noted that he had managed almost 28 matches, recording 19 wins, four defeats and four draws, but admitted that the defeat to South Africa came at a crucial stage.

Madugu blamed Nigeria’s failure to convert chances and defensive mistakes for the loss.

“We had chances, but conversion was another problem. We also made some little errors at the back, and they capitalised on that and got their goals,” he said.

He also suggested that complacency and overconfidence may have contributed to the team’s costly mistakes.

“It could be complacency, it could also be overconfidence, and then we end up making mistakes over unnecessary issues,” he added.

Madugu further admitted that the Super Falcons were wasteful in front of goal despite creating several opportunities during the tournament.

“We have not been clinical in front of goal. We create several chances, but we are very wasteful with the opportunities that come our way,” he said.

According to him, Nigeria could have put the game beyond South Africa’s reach in the first half but failed to take their chances.

“South Africa were more clinical and converted the chances that came their way,” Madugu added.

World.title: Maresca uncertain over Rodri’s future at Man City
World.content:
Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca said “anything can happen” amid reports La Liga champions Barcelona have bid to sign World Cup winner Rodri.

City are understood to have rejected an opening bid of £38.5 million ($52 million) from Barcelona for the midfielder.

The 30-year-old has just one season remaining on his deal at the Etihad and has been strongly linked with a return to his native Spain.

City are reported to want about £68 million for Rodri, who was named player of the tournament at the recent World Cup in North America.

Barcelona could now come back with an increased offer for Rodri, which in turn may lead to a City move for Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez.

Rodri was the last City player to report for pre-season training, only arriving back on Friday, having had back surgery after starring in Spain’s World Cup triumph.

“First of all, we already said the transfer window is open, we can buy and sell players, anything can happen,” Maresca told a press conference on Friday ahead of this weekend’s Community Shield clash against Arsenal.

“I just saw Rodri now in the building, I gave him a big hug. He looks good, so we’ll see what happens.”

Maresca added he would not speak about players under contract at other clubs, but said City still have work to do in the final weeks of the summer transfer window.

“For sure there are things we need to do,” he said. “Now, how many, I don’t know. It can be one, can be two, it depends also if players are going to leave.”

Rodri joined City from Atletico Madrid in 2019. He won multiple Premier League titles and the 2023 Champions League under former boss Pep Guardiola.

He also won Euro 2024 and that year’s Ballon d’Or before a serious knee injury sidelined him for much of the 2024/25 campaign.

Chelsea are reported to have set a Friday deadline concerning an offer for Fernandez but Maresca, asked if that meant City would put in a bid later in the day, said: “Not today to be honest, I don’t think we’re going to do something today.”

– Reijnders on the way out –

City have already spent £116 million on England’s Elliot Anderson following Bernardo Silva’s exit, but fellow midfielder Tijjani Reijnders is on the verge of joining Saudi club Al Qadsiah in a deal estimated to be worth £51 million.

Reijnders only arrived from AC Milan for £46.5 million last year, but started just half of City’s Premier League matches.

Maresca said that it was “normal” a player would want to play more games.

“Tijjani’s situation is like James Trafford’s situation, some more players, but I think when the club, the player, the manager, they all think the same way, that probably the best decision for a player is to go, you have to go.”

The Community Shield pits the winners of last season’s Premier League, Arsenal, against FA Cup holders City.

Arsenal finished seven points ahead of second-placed City as they ended their 22-year wait for a Premier League title last term and Maresca vowed his men would do all they could to close the gap to Mikel Arteta’s men this season.

“Arsenal have shown in the last two or three or four, five years, that they are always there,” said Maresca. “It is a fantastic team from Mikel.

“They won the Premier League, they showed how good they are in this moment. But at the same time, we are City and we’re going to try to close the gap and compete.”

AFP

World.title: Police parade 14 kidnap suspects, recover 5 AK-47 rifles, 310 rounds in Enugu
World.content:
By Chinedu Adonu

ENUGU — The Enugu State Police Command has paraded 14 suspected members of a kidnapping syndicate allegedly linked to several kidnapping operations and a murder case across the state.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Mamman Bitrus Giwa, disclosed this on Thursday during a press briefing at the Command headquarters, GRA, Enugu, saying the suspects were arrested through intelligence-led operations conducted across several states.

Giwa said the operations led to the recovery of five AK-47 rifles, two pump-action guns, one locally fabricated firearm, 310 rounds of live 7.62 x 39mm ammunition, eight cartridges and seven empty AK-47 magazines.

He said two of the suspects allegedly involved in the kidnapping of worshippers at a church in Inoyi, Affa community, Udi Local Government Area, fled to Port Harcourt but were subsequently traced and arrested.

According to him, preliminary investigations showed that after fleeing Enugu, the suspects regrouped with their associates in Port Harcourt and kidnapped another victim, who was released after a N5 million ransom was paid.

The CP said the 14 suspects were linked to a wider criminal network operating across different parts of the country, with members converging in Enugu to plan and execute kidnapping operations before returning to their respective locations.

“The suspects had confessed to involvement in several kidnapping incidents along the Enugu-Ugwuogo-Opi-Nsukka Road, Obioma-9th Mile-Umulumgbe-Ukpatu axis, Eke-Affa-Egede-Ezinze axis and other locations in Ezeagu Local Government Area,” the CP said.

Giwa disclosed that the suspects had been linked to the abduction of a man at Mgbabuowa/Aguobuowa, Ezeagu, on May 25, 2026, for which N5.5 million ransom was allegedly collected.

He added that the gang was also linked to the abduction of two men and the shooting and killing of a woman at Obioma, Udi, on May 9, during which $28,700 was allegedly obtained as ransom.

The suspects were further linked to the abduction of two victims along the Eke-Ezinze Road, Udi, on April 10, for which $70,000 was allegedly paid as ransom, as well as the kidnapping of seven victims at Obinaofia, Ezeagu, on April 12, for which N25 million was allegedly collected.

The police boss said investigations further revealed that proceeds from the alleged criminal activities were laundered through investments in livestock and properties, lavish spending and overseas trips.

“The arrests and recoveries are a clear demonstration of the effectiveness of sustained intelligence gathering, ICT-enabled investigation, inter-agency collaboration, inter-state cooperation and coordinated operational policing adopted by the Command,” Giwa said.

He said investigations were ongoing to identify other members of the syndicate, recover more firearms and criminal proceeds, and establish the suspects’ involvement in other kidnapping and violent-crime cases within and outside Enugu State.

Giwa assured residents that the Command would sustain its offensive against kidnapping, armed robbery, murder, cultism and other violent crimes.

“We will continue to make Enugu State increasingly unconducive to unrepentant local criminals, criminal elements seeking to infiltrate the State, and their activities,” he said.

He appealed to members of the public to remain vigilant and to provide the police with timely information on suspicious persons, movements and activities.

“I therefore urge residents to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious persons, movements and activities through established Police channels,” he said.

Giwa also commended the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, Enugu State Governor, Dr. Peter Ndubuisi Mbah, and other security agencies for their support and collaboration in the fight against crime.

World.title: Police arrest 29-yr-old man for desecrating Qur’an for ritual in Zuru
World.content:
File image.

By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi

The Kebbi State Police Command has arrested one Abubakar Musa, male, 29, of Rafin Mose Village, Zuru LGA, in connection with a case of criminal conspiracy, abuse of religious books, use of spells and hypnosis, and inciting disturbance.

Kebbi Police Command spokesperson, SP Bashir Usman, in a statement on Friday, said the incident occurred on 9th August 2026 at about 1900hrs in the Zango Area, Zuru.

According to him, preliminary investigation revealed that the suspect allegedly conspired with two others; Rabi’u Tela, husband of Zarau Hassan, and Hamza Zango, both now at large, to dig a pit inside Zarau Hassan’s room and bury therein a copy of the Holy Qur’an, together with semen, white and red kolanuts, underwear, dead animals, and other fetish items.

The act was allegedly intended to make Zarau Hassan more submissive to her husband, Rabi’u Tela, and was carried out in circumstances capable of provoking a breach of the peace among the Muslim faithful in the community.

However, efforts are ongoing to apprehend the two fleeing suspects, while Abubakar Musa remains in police custody and will be charged in court upon conclusion of the investigation.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Umar M. Hadejia, strongly condemns the alleged act and warns that the Command will deal decisively, within the law, with individuals whose actions threaten religious harmony, public order, and peaceful coexistence.

Members of the public are urged to promptly report suspicious activities to the Police through as they will be treated with utmost confidentiality.

World.title: At Washington Talks, Nigeria Reinforces Defence, Security Partnership with US
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Federal Government has reinforced its defence and security partnership with the United States Government with a view to deepening military-to-military relations and strengthening counter-terrorism cooperation between Nigeria and the United States.

The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), stated this during a high-level bilateral engagement with the United States Government in Washington, D.C.

During a strategic meeting at the Pentagon, the Defence Minister was joined by a high-powered Nigerian delegation that included the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele; the Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede; the Chief of Defence Intelligence, Lt Gen Parker Udiandeye; and other senior officers from the Armed Forces of Nigeria.

According to a statement by the Special Assistant on Media to the Minister of Defence, Leah Katung-Babatunde, the Nigerian delegation held robust discussions with senior cabinet officials of the U.S. Department of War, led by the Acting Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary of War for International Security Affairs, Julia Sokol.

The engagement, she said, served as a direct continuation of the United States-Nigeria Joint Working Group Defence Bilateral Talks, focusing on shared security architecture, intelligence collaboration and operational synergies.

Mrs Katung-Babatunde said the diplomatic mission, led by the National Security Adviser (NSA), Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, was made up of senior government officials who were in the United States of America for the second meeting of the US-Nigeria Joint Working Group, held from 12 to 13 August 2026.

Co-chaired by Mallam Nuhu Ribadu and Allison Hooker, the U.S. Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs, the meeting reviewed actionable progress and strategic frameworks following Nigeria’s designation as a Country of Particular Concern (CPC).

“Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to sustained dialogue, mutual respect and strategic alliance in combating global and regional threats,” the statement said.

World.title: Adegoke Remains Oyo ADC Guber Candidate, Says Media Team
World.content:
Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

The Media Team of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate in Oyo State, Adegboyega Taofeek Adegoke, on Friday, described the claim to the party’s governorship ticket by one of the gubernatorial aspirants, Mr. Gbemileke Alagbe, as “wishful thinking”.

This is just as it questioned how Alagbe could claim to be the ADC governorship candidate after instituting a suit against the party and its National Working Committee (NWC).

Alagbe had on Thursday during a press conference stated that he is the ADC candidate in the 2027 general election, and unveiled Mr. Niyi Aborisade as his running mate and deputy governorship candidate.

But the media team cited Suit No. FHC/IB/CS/67/2026, filed by him at the Federal High Court in Ibadan on June 28, 2026, stating that the case had been adjourned until September 15, 2026.

“How can someone that has already taken the ADC, the ADC NWC and others to court be claiming he is the governorship candidate submitted by the same party, ADC, to INEC? Is that not a contradiction?” the team asked.

It also questioned the basis of Alagbe’s decision to sue the party and subsequently claim that the same party had submitted his name to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

It maintained that Adegoke emerged as the ADC governorship candidate at the party’s primary election with 16,051 votes.

According to the team, the primary election results, which were publicly reported by multiple media organisations, showed Bisi Ilaka with 11,415 votes, Alagbe with 241 votes, Azeez Adeduntan with 155 votes and Aborisade with 67 votes.

It therefore urged the media, members of the public and ADC members in the state to disregard what it described as false claims concerning the party’s governorship ticket.

It said: “The identity of a political party’s candidate is not determined by who makes the loudest declaration or who receives the most publicity. It is determined by the applicable electoral process, authentic records and the law.

“For the avoidance of doubt, Olooye Adegboyega Taofeek Adegoke remains our recognised gubernatorial candidate, and we remain firmly committed to defending his mandate through every lawful and legitimate avenue available to us.

“We have no objection to any individual exercising his or her lawful rights, but we will strongly resist any attempt to substitute propaganda, wishful thinking, or unverifiable claims for established facts.”

World.title: Tinubu To INEC, Security Agencies: Ensure Peaceful, Transparent Poll In Osun
World.content:
* Says outcome of Osun election must reflect will of the citizenry

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and the security agencies to ensure a peaceful and transparent election in Osun State.

The people of Osun State will go to the polls on Saturday, August 15, 2026, to elect their governor in an election where 15 candidates are contesting.

Among them are the incumbent Governor Ademola Adeleke, the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Asiwaju Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji, and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) candidate, Hon. Najeem Salaam.

The president, in a release issued on Friday by his Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, also charged the electorate in Osun State to come out to discharge their civic responsibility and eschew any act that could disrupt the peaceful conduct of the election, while assuring the people of their safety before and after the polls.

“As the people of Osun State head to the polling units to elect who will govern them in the next four years, I call on the Independent National Electoral Commission to ensure orderly conduct of the election. The election must be transparent, free and fair. I urge INEC to ensure the integrity of the process,” Tinubu said.

“INEC must use this last off-cycle election as a test case to demonstrate to Nigerians their full preparedness for the 2027 polls,” he added.

“I have charged the Inspector-General of Police and other heads of security outfits taking part in the election to provide maximum security at polling units. No room should be allowed for troublemakers to disrupt the process.

“Electoral officials and voters must be protected so they can perform their civic duties without fear or intimidation.

“Voters should feel confident to go out in their numbers to vote for the candidate of their choice as all measures necessary to ensure a peaceful, free and fair election have been put in place.

“Our elections must be credible, and the outcome of the Osun governorship election must reflect the will of the people,” the president declared.

World.title: RATTAWU Extols Adeola Ajayi’s Integrity, Competence, Applauds Tinubu for Appointing Him as DSS DG
World.content:
The Radio, Television, Theatre and Arts Workers Union (RATTAWU) has applauded President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for appointing Mr Adeola Oluwatosin Ajayi as the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), describing him as a man of valour, integrity, competence and proven capacity.

The commendation was made by the RATTAWU President, Comrade Prince Emeka Kalu, during the union’s Media/Security critical engagement and strategic partnership for national development.

During the engagement, the DSS Director-General was conferred with the Golden Era Pillar of Critical and Strategic Intelligence for National Development Award.

The initiative is designed to recognise individuals and institutions that have made outstanding contributions to national development, security, democracy, culture and the growth of Nigeria.

Speaking during the visit, Kalu commended President Tinubu for appointing Ajayi to lead the nation’s foremost domestic intelligence organisation.

He described the DSS Director-General as a silent achiever, a competent and detribalised Nigerian and a man whose commitment to national service transcends ethnic, religious and political considerations.

According to the RATTAWU President, the appointment demonstrates the importance of placing capable Nigerians with integrity and professional competence in strategic positions of national responsibility.

He further noted that the role of the DSS in protecting Nigeria’s National interests, gathering critical intelligence and supporting National security cannot be overemphasised, particularly at a time when the Country is confronted with complex security and emerging technological challenges.

Kalu said RATTAWU, as a Union representing workers across the radio, television, theatre and arts sectors, has a responsibility to contribute to National development by using its platforms to promote responsible communication, peace, unity and democratic values.

He stated that RATTAWU Nigeria would continue to provide platforms for the sensitisation of citizens, especially as the nation prepares for the forthcoming general election.

He stressed that the media and creative sectors have an important role to play in combating misinformation, promoting tolerance and encouraging citizens to participate responsibly in the democratic process.

Kalu also emphasised the need for stronger collaboration between security agencies, the media, creative professionals and organised labour in building a peaceful and cohesive Nigeria.

Responding, the DSS Director-General expressed appreciation to the leadership of RATTAWU for the exceptional honour bestowed on him.

He described the recognition as a significant gesture that would further encourage him and the Service to remain committed to their responsibilities to the nation.

Ajayi encouraged RATTAWU to remain steadfast in upholding values that promote national cohesion, tolerance, peace and unity, noting that such values are essential to the continued stability and development of Nigeria.

He assured the Union of his willingness to remain available for constructive engagement, particularly in areas that could create meaningful networks, partnerships and collaboration between the DSS and RATTAWU.

The Director-General expressed optimism that such engagements would strengthen institutional cooperation and contribute to greater national cohesion.

World.title: Security Chiefs, Katsina Govt Intensify War against Banditry, Terrorism
World.content:
Francis Sardauna in Katsina

Security chiefs, Katsina State Government and other stakeholders in the state have called for stronger synergy, intelligence sharing, and coordinated operations among security agencies to defeat terrorism, banditry and other criminal activities threatening the Northwest region of the country.

The call was made at the North-west Conference of State Directors of Security held in Katsina yesterday with the theme: ‘Unite Against Terror.’

Speaking at the conference, the Katsina State Director of the Department of State Services (DSS), Alhassan Iliyasu, said there’s collaboration among security agencies, communities and other stakeholders to effectively tackle terrorism, banditry and other criminal activities in the region.

He said the fight against terrorism and banditry could not be won by security agencies alone, stressing that every member of society had a role to play in providing useful information and supporting security operations to tackle the region’s evolving security challenges.

He added that the conference provided an opportunity for heads of intelligence-led organisations and security agencies across the region to review emerging threats, share experiences and develop renewed strategies for curbing banditry and related criminal activities.

Iliyasu said: “The purpose of this conference is for us to come together, review the nitty-gritty of the security challenges, come up with renewed strategies and scale up our countermeasures.”

He noted that the collaboration among security agencies, community-based security structures, vigilante groups and other stakeholders would significantly improve responses to security threats across the northwest region of the country.

He commended the Director-General of the DSS, Mr. Adeola Oluwatosin Ajayi, for providing renewed direction for the Service and creating opportunities to strengthen its intelligence and tactical capabilities.

On his part, the Commander, 17 Brigade, Nigerian Army, Katsina, Brigadier-General Ishaya Ibrahim, explained that the synergy among security agencies was no longer an advantage but an imperative in confronting the evolving and borderless nature of terrorism.

He disclosed that military firepower and territorial operations alone could not defeat terrorists, adding that actionable intelligence remained critical to the success of military operations.

He said terrorists exploit gaps in information, coordination and trust, hence the need for the nation’s security agencies to bridge such gaps through real-time intelligence sharing, joint operational planning and mutual support.

In his opening remarks, Governor Dikko Umaru Radda said Katsina State had recorded significant improvements in its security challenges through a combination of both kinetic and non-kinetic measures.

Represented by his Deputy, Faruk Lawal, the governor attributed the security improvement in the state to the cooperation between conventional security agencies and the state’s home-grown security initiative, the Community Watch Corps.

He added that the state government had also “invested heavily” in non-kinetic interventions aimed at addressing some of the socio-economic factors that could fuel insecurity in the state.

The governor, therefore, appealed to security agencies and the media to be strategic in communicating security-related developments, warning against reports that could inadvertently amplify the activities of bandits and other criminal elements.

Radda urged the media to support security efforts by providing responsible coverage capable of boosting public confidence and the morale of security personnel operating in the northwest region of the country.

World.title: If OPay Is Going Public, Nigeria Should Be on the Ticket
World.content:
Shola Akande

If Bloomberg’s reporting proves correct, OPay could ring a bell in New York before the end of the year. The payments company, built on Nigerian consumers, Nigerian agents and Nigerian transactions, has reportedly engaged Citigroup, Deutsche Bank and JPMorgan for a potential United States listing targeting a valuation of around $4 billion.

That would be good news. It would be a powerful validation of what many of us have argued for years: Nigeria can produce businesses capable of competing for global capital at the highest level.

Nobody should begrudge OPay the deep capital pools, analyst coverage and international visibility that a New York listing can provide. Those advantages are real. But they should prompt a second question, rather than close the conversation.

Why not both?

A dual listing, New York for global capital and Lagos for the home market, is not a sentimental proposition. It is a commercial one. And the case rests on four things: customers, domestic liquidity, precedent and alignment.

The first is the customer.

OPay’s reported tens of millions of users are overwhelmingly Nigerian. They are the traders, artisans, students, small businesses and salary earners whose transactions helped build the franchise. A secondary listing on the Nigerian Exchange would give some of those customers the opportunity to become shareholders, converting economic participation into ownership.

Nigeria has already seen what happens when a major consumer-facing company deliberately broadens domestic ownership. MTN Nigeria’s public offer attracted more than 126,000 retail investors and created tens of thousands of new market accounts. The lesson is not that every shareholder becomes a brand ambassador. It is that a strong Nigerian consumer franchise can generate substantial domestic investor interest.

The second is liquidity.

Nigeria’s capital market is not the market it was a few years ago. The banking recapitalisation has demonstrated the depth of domestic institutional capital, while pension assets have continued to expand. The Exchange now has dedicated indices designed to support institutional investment, including the NGX Pension and NGX Pension Broad indices.

That matters because the argument for Lagos is no longer simply that Nigerians would like to own OPay. There is a potentially meaningful pool of domestic capital that could actually buy it.

Nigeria’s market infrastructure has also moved forward. The shift to T+1 settlement brought the equities settlement cycle in line with foreign markets including New York, reducing one important source of operational friction for international investors.

A Lagos listing would also give OPay access to naira-denominated demand and, depending on its eventual size and index eligibility, potentially broaden institutional demand through relevant domestic benchmarks. That is not a substitute for New York’s deeper pools of global capital. It is an additional source of liquidity and ownership.

The third is precedent. This road has been walked before.

Seplat has maintained a Lagos and London dual listing since 2014. Airtel Africa listed in London and subsequently in Lagos in 2019. Both demonstrated that a company can use an international market for global capital and visibility while retaining a meaningful connection to its home market.

The point is not that OPay should copy either company. It is that the supposed choice between international capital and domestic ownership is not a choice at all. The two can coexist.

The fourth is alignment.

OPay operates within Nigeria’s regulated payments ecosystem. The Central Bank of Nigeria lists OPay Digital Services as a licensed mobile money operator, while the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation lists it among insured mobile money operators. Its regulatory relationships, agent network and core customer base are deeply Nigerian. That creates a natural commercial argument for maintaining a visible presence in the country’s capital market.

But there is an important concession to make.

New York may well be the right primary market for OPay.

A company seeking a multibillion-dollar valuation may reasonably conclude that New York offers the deepest pool of fintech investors, the strongest international analyst coverage, the broadest universe of comparable companies and the most efficient access to global capital. If that is the conclusion, it should not be treated as a failure of the Nigerian market.

It should simply make the case for Lagos more precise.

Lagos does not need to beat New York. It needs to complement it.

A secondary Nigerian listing would allow OPay to establish a domestic ownership base without sacrificing the advantages of its international listing. New York could serve as the primary venue for global price discovery and international liquidity; Lagos could provide local institutional participation, retail ownership and a direct connection to the market in which much of the company’s economic story was created.

The two markets are complements, not competitors.

Some will argue that a dual listing creates additional compliance costs and administrative complexity. That is true. But it is precisely why the Nigerian market must continue making itself easier to access and operate in. Faster settlement, better market infrastructure, more efficient foreign-exchange processes and broader institutional participation are not cosmetic reforms. They determine whether companies view a domestic listing as a commercial decision or a patriotic sacrifice.

That distinction matters.

Because there is a bigger issue here than OPay’s eventual cap table.

Nigeria is entering a period in which some of its most successful businesses may begin contemplating the public markets. If the pattern becomes that our strongest companies build much of their scale here but list and raise their most consequential capital elsewhere, Nigeria risks exporting not just companies, but the wealth-creation opportunities attached to them.

The answer is not to compel companies to list at home. Nor is it to complain when founders and investors choose the markets that best serve their interests.

The answer is to make Nigeria’s capital market so competitive that listing here becomes the rational commercial choice.

Much of that work is already underway.

That is why OPay’s potential listing presents an opportunity beyond one company. It can become a test of whether Nigeria is prepared to capture more of the value created by the businesses emerging from its economy.

And it can set a precedent for the generation of Nigerian fintechs behind it: Moniepoint, Flutterwave and others that may eventually face similar decisions about accessing the public markets.

So this is not a criticism of OPay. It is an invitation to think bigger about what a successful public-market debut could look like.

Ring the bell in New York by all means, but there is a compelling case for ringing one in Lagos too.

The market is ready. The capital is waiting. And millions of Nigerians who already use the platform every day should have the opportunity, if they choose, to become owners of the company they helped build.

That would not be madness.

That would be the whole point.

* Akande, an economist, writes from Lagos

World.title: Let Ballot, Not Violence, Decide Osun Election, IPCR Warns
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The Institute for Peace and Conflict Resolution (IPCR) has warned political actors in Osun State against allowing violence, intimidation and inflammatory rhetoric to overshadow Saturday’s governorship election, urging all stakeholders to ensure that the ballot, rather than coercion, determines the choice of the people.

The warning came on Friday, less than 24 hours before voters in the state are scheduled to elect their governor, amid heightened concerns over election-related violence and security threats in parts of the state.

Recent security assessment have identified several Osun local government areas as vulnerable to electoral violence.

In a press statement by its Director-General, Dr. Joseph Ochogwu, the IPCR charged governorship candidates, political parties, their supporters, security agencies, election officials and voters to place the interest of Osun above partisan considerations.

The institute cautioned that political competition must not degenerate into violence, intimidation, threats, hate speech or destruction of property, stressing that political contests are temporary while the consequences of electoral violence could scar individuals, families and communities for years.

“Elections should not be treated as a do-or-die affair,” the Institute said, urging political leaders and candidates to demonstrate leadership by cautioning their supporters against inflammatory statements, misinformation and actions capable of escalating tensions.

The IPCR also delivered a clear message to candidates who may be dissatisfied with the outcome: accept the result peacefully or seek redress through the courts, rather than resorting to self-help.

It urged the candidates and political parties to respect the rules of democratic competition and demonstrate maturity before, during and after the election.

The institute equally called on voters to resist attempts by politicians or other actors to recruit them as agents of violence, urging them to exercise their civic responsibilities peacefully and respect the rights of citizens supporting rival political parties.

It advised voters to maintain order at polling units, respect election officials and security personnel, and avoid confrontations with political opponents.

The IPCR further warned citizens against becoming conduits for election-related misinformation, particularly on social media, urging them to verify information before sharing rumours or unconfirmed reports capable of triggering unrest.

The appeal comes against a backdrop of heightened tension in Osun, where reports of shootings, killings, clashes and other politically linked disturbances have fuelled concerns over the security of the August 15 poll.

A recent assessment by The Kukah Centre identified 15 local government areas as critical, high or moderate violence-risk zones, with Osogbo and Irewole classified as critical-risk areas.

The IPCR consequently charged security agencies to remain professional, impartial and respectful of citizens’ rights while ensuring adequate protection for voters, election officials and electoral materials.

It also called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and its officials to discharge their responsibilities transparently and impartially, ensuring that eligible voters can cast their ballots without fear or intimidation.

Beyond the polling booths, the institute urged traditional rulers, religious leaders, community leaders, civil society organisations and the media to play their part in preventing violence and discouraging inflammatory rhetoric.

It stressed that the responsibility for a peaceful election does not rest solely with security agencies or INEC, but with every stakeholder participating in the electoral process.

The institute placed particular emphasis on the period after the announcement of results, urging winners to be magnanimous in victory and losers to accept defeat peacefully or pursue legitimate grievances through the judicial process.

The warning is particularly significant as Osun heads into Saturday’s contest after political parties had earlier signed a peace accord committing themselves to peaceful, free and credible elections.

The IPCR therefore called on the people of Osun State to protect the peace of their communities and demonstrate democratic maturity by ensuring that political differences do not become a trigger for bloodshed.

It said the ultimate test of the election would be whether the people are allowed to freely choose their governor without violence, intimidation or coercion.

“Let the ballot, rather than violence, intimidation or coercion, determine the choice of the people,” the Institute urged.

World.title: Ex-IGP Adamu Empowers 2,800 Farmers In Nasarawa
World.content:
Igbawase Ukumba in Lafia

No fewer than 2,800 farmers from the Western Senatorial Zone of Nasarawa State have benefited from an agricultural intervention programme initiated by former Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Mohammed Adamu.

The empowerment programme, which involved distribution of fertilisers, modern farm implements and compensation to farmers, was flagged off on Friday in Karu Local Government Area of the state.

The zone comprises five local government areas – Keffi, Karu, Kokona, Nasarawa and Toto.

Speaking at the ceremony, the former IGP, convener of the IGP Group, said the intervention was aimed at complementing government efforts to achieve food security and uplift rural livelihoods.

“We are here to support our farmers. We are here to compensate our farmers. We are here to modernise our farming method. We are here to introduce implements that will aid in producing more food for our people,” he said.

Adamu disclosed that the Karu exercise covered the Western Zone, adding that a similar gesture would be extended to farmers in Nasarawa North Senatorial District.

According to him, the initiative is a token to encourage farming activities and boost food supply in the state.

He called on well-meaning individuals and corporate organisations to support farmers.

“If you have the means, please come out and also assist the farmers. Come out of the little that you have to assist the farmers. Because when you assist them, we are going to get more food. If you have more food in the market, the food will be cheap and everybody will get it,” he stated.

He further revealed that plans were underway to extend similar support to women in small-scale businesses and youths in the state.

“Today, we are doing this for the farmers. We have plans for the small-scale business women and the youth. We are also going to undertake that,” he added.

The former IGP noted that although government was doing its best, it could not meet all the needs of the people, hence the need for private support.

“We know the government is trying its best to provide for the people of Nasarawa but we know they will never be able to do for everybody. So there is nothing that we are competing with them. We are only contributing our quota,” he said.

In his welcome address, the Chairman, Nasarawa State All Farmers Association of Nigeria (AFAN), Ambassador Isaac Kugbu, represented by Isah Buba, the state coordinator of AFAN, lauded Adamu for the intervention, describing it as an exemplary leadership and a timely move that would boost food production.

Speaking on behalf of farmers in the zone, he said: “No farmer, no food, no nation.”

He expressed gratitude to the former IGP, noting that the intervention was not the first of its kind and that farmers in the zone had continued to benefit from his consistent support for agriculture and food security.

He said the gesture was worthy of emulation by other well-meaning Nigerians.

The chairman confirmed the presence of all five AFAN local government chairmen in the Western Zone, including chairmen of Nasarawa, Kokona, Karu and Keffi LGAs, led by M.S. Mariga, Mr. Danyan, Ladidi Amba and Alhaji Alba respectively.

THISDAY reports that distribution commenced immediately after the flag-off, with Toto LGA taken first because of its distance.

The beneficiaries, who were visibly elated, commended the organisers for the timely intervention.

World.title: Nine-hour power outage to hit parts of Durban
World.content:
Residents in 12 Durban areas are warned of a planned electricity outage next week. Image: canva

Residents in parts of Durban’s Outer West are being warned of a planned electricity outage on Monday, 17 August, as the eThekwini Electricity and Energy Directorate carries out work at the Waterfall Substation.

The planned interruption will take place from 8:00 to 17:00 and is required to allow technicians to test and commission the transformer protection scheme at the substation.

Several areas will be affected by the outage.



Areas affected by the planned power outage

The following areas could experience an interruption to their electricity supply:

Berrell

Congo

Crestholme

Crestview

Lower Molweni

Luthele

Maromeni

Nkangala

Nogxaza

Tin Town

Umngeni

Waterfall

Residents in these areas are urged to plan and make the necessary arrangements before the electricity is switched off.

The municipality has advised that customers who have not been switched off by 8.30 can assume that they will not be affected by the planned outage.

Residents urged to take precautions

As with any power outage, residents are advised to take precautions and ensure that appliances are switched off before the outage begins.

The public is also warned to treat all electrical installations as live throughout the outage.

The planned work is necessary to test and commission the transformer protection scheme at Waterfall Substation, which forms part of the municipality’s electricity infrastructure.



The planned outage is scheduled to run until 17:00 on Monday, 17 August.

World.title: El Niño heatwave, or an El Niño water crisis?
World.content:
South Africa's dams look healthy today, but a strengthening El Niño could change that fast this summer: Image ChatGPT

The El Niño water risk is what readers pushed back on when we covered South Africa’s shift from this week’s cold snap toward a strengthening El Niño, insisting heat isn’t really the concern…

Water is.

Here’s what the data actually says about that risk.



Why the El Niño water risk matters more than healthy dam levels suggest

As of early August, South Africa’s dams sit at a reassuring 95.9% full nationally, with the Western Cape’s average at 79.6% and North West leading at 102.4%.

But climate researchers warn that healthy dam levels now say very little about what a strong El Niño summer could do to them.

Extreme heat dramatically accelerates evaporation, acting like a sponge that pulls untreated water straight out of open dams and reservoirs, often without a single drop reaching a tap or a field.



Why El Niño hits South Africa’s water system twice over

El Niño typically brings both delayed rainfall and higher temperatures to South Africa’s summer rainfall regions, a combination that compounds rather than simply adds up.

Underground aquifers recharge slowly, so sustained dry spells can cause boreholes to run dry or turn saline.

The World Meteorological Organisation’s latest seasonal update shows sea surface temperatures in the key Niño 3.4 region climbing toward roughly 2.9°C above average by October, with the event expected to peak around November.



Exactly as South Africa heads into the heart of summer.

The Day Zero comparison experts keep bringing up

Cape Town’s 2018 Day Zero crisis is the reference point climate experts keep returning to, a reminder of how quickly healthy-looking dam levels can unravel under sustained heat and low rainfall.

Farmers, agribusinesses and municipalities are already being urged to build in buffer capacity now, rather than waiting for restrictions to force the issue later in the season.



It’s easy to look at 95% full dams and think we’re in the clear, hey, but if this El Niño plays out the way forecasters expect, that number could look very different by autumn.

2018 was hectic, I really hope we don’t see a repeat of that in 2026.

Do you think water restrictions are a bigger risk than the heat itself this summer?



Let us know in the comments below, Mzansi…

World.title: Zambia stops election vote count amid violence fears
World.content:
Zambia has suspended the counting and announcement of election results nationwide after the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) reported violence targeting polling staff and the alleged theft of marked ballot papers.

The commission announced the suspension on Friday, a day after Zambians voted in presidential, parliamentary and local government elections.

The nation held presidential, parliamentary and local government elections on Thursday.



The ECZ said it had received reports of violence “during the counting and announcement of results in some districts”.

It said the violence was “targeted at Poll staff” and, in some cases, had resulted in “the theft of marked ballot papers in ballot boxes”.

The commission said it had acted because of the security situation and continued threats of violence.



“In view of the security situation and continued threats of violence,” the ECZ said it had “with immediate effect suspended the counting and announcement of results throughout the country”.

The commission cited Section 67 (3) of the Electoral Process Act No. 35 of 2016 as the legal basis for the suspension.

Electoral Commission of Zambia to review suspension

The suspension has put the brakes on the counting process as Zambia waits for the outcome of a closely watched presidential election.



The said it would review the decision within 24 hours.

“The Commission will review the suspension within 24 hours,” it said.

Counting began shortly after polling stations closed on Thursday, but no official presidential results had been announced when the commission halted the process.



The ECZ had previously expected to complete the announcement of the presidential results by Monday.

Opposition raises concerns over delays

The suspension came shortly after opposition candidate Brian Mundubile expressed “grave concern” over delays in announcing the presidential results.

Mundubile warned that prolonged delays could create opportunities for interference or manipulation.



He also cited what he described as “deeply troubling reports” from several areas, including alleged military involvement at tallying centres and concerns about the movement of ballot boxes.

Mundubile called for the immediate publication of results on a polling-station-by-polling-station basis.

He also called for the protection of the chain of custody of ballot materials and investigations into the reported incidents.



Hichilema urges Zambians to remain calm

President Hakainde Hichilema, who is seeking a second five-year term, has urged Zambians to remain calm while the electoral authorities handle the situation.

Hichilema faces 13 challengers, with Mundubile regarded as one of his main opponents.

The president urged citizens to remain “peaceful, patient and patriotic” as they await the official outcome from the authorities managing the election.



The ECZ’s decision has now created uncertainty over when Zambia will receive the official election results, with the commission first needing to assess the security situation before deciding whether to resume counting.

World.title: The R19 billion Powerball winner nobody will likely ever meet
World.content:
Someone in Illinois won a R19 billion ($1.04 billion) Powerball jackpot and may never be publicly identified: Image ChatGPT

This billion dollar Powerball winner is somewhere in Illinois, holding a ticket worth R19 billion ($1.04 billion), and there’s a real chance the world never finds out who they are.

The winning ticket was sold at a Hy-Vee Fast & Fresh petrol station in Quincy, Illinois on Wednesday, 12 August after 44 consecutive draws without a winner.

The numbers drawn were 4, 26, 66, 67 and 69, plus Powerball 9.



It’s the eighth-largest Powerball jackpot in the game’s history, and the winner has up to a year to come forward and claim it.

Why this billion dollar Powerball winner could disappear completely

Illinois law allows any lottery winner claiming a prize over $250 000 to request anonymity.

To do so, they must correctly submit a written claim form asking that officials keep their name and hometown confidential.



If the winner doesn’t submit the form, or fills it out incorrectly, officials can release their details anyway.

Illinois is one of 19 US states offering at least partial anonymity to winners, a stark contrast to states like Florida, where winners’ names become public record.

South Africans actually have it easier

South African winners don’t need to navigate a patchwork of state laws to protect their privacy.



Sizekhaya, the operator running the National Lottery since 1 June 2026, allows Lotto and PowerBall winners to remain anonymous by default if they choose, no special form or legal loophole required.

It’s one of the reasons South Africa rarely sees the kind of speculation and manhunt-style coverage that follows a jackpot like this one in the US.

What the winner is actually walking away with

The jackpot can be taken as 30 payments over 29 years which increases by 5% each year, or a lump sum of roughly $450.5 million (R8.4 billion) before tax.



Most winners choose the lump sum, and most take weeks to come forward while lawyers, financial advisors and tax planners get everything in place first.

Eish, imagine being this billion dollar Powerball winner and just… not telling anyone yet. That takes a level of patience I don’t think I have.

Click here to view past PowerBall and PowerBall XTRA results and payouts.



Would you want your name made public if you won a jackpot like this, or would you rather stay anonymous like Sizekhaya allows here?

World.title: Sundowns train with Kaizer Chiefs’ Kappa ball, but is it unusual?
World.content:
Mamelodi Sundowns are preparing for their Saturday’s visit to the FNB Stadium where they will face Kaizer Chiefs in the Betway Premiership.

Kick-off is at 15:00.

And in preparation for that match, the Brazilians were pictured conducting their training sessions using Amakhosi’s Kappa ball.



But is this something unusual or is there anything wrong with what Sundowns did?

This piece answers that question…

Also read: Kaizer Chiefs without EIGHT top stars for Sundowns clash

SUNDOWNS USE KAIZER CHIEFS’ KAPPA BALL FOR TRAINING, BUT IS IT WRONG?

The Kappa ball is Chiefs‘ official match ball for all their home games, and the ball is custom-branded and FIFA-approved.

What this means is that the Kappa ball is not exclusive to their training sessions only as opposition will still get to use it on matchday.

Now, when Sundowns or any team prepares to face Chiefs at their home ground, using their official match ball is standard practice.



Also read | Miguel’s warning to Sundowns: We are Kaizer Chiefs, we fear no one!

A visiting team is more than allowed to train with the home’s official match ball or anything equivalent days before the actual match is NOT unusual.

This is to allow players to get used to its flight, weight, and bounce ahead of kick-off, and as things stand, there is no existing PSL rule that prohibits the visiting team from using the home side’s official ball.

In fact, experts describe this as proper and good preparation, and it would have been ignorant of Sundowns not do so given the magnitude of this fixture.

World.title: UK buyers pay record R15.9 million for Cape Town penthouse
World.content:
Foreign buyers are once again showing strong interest in the Cape Town property market. Image: canva / The Marlow on Mill

A penthouse in a brand-new apartment development in Newlands, Cape Town, has been sold for a record R15.9 million, with the buyers travelling from the UK to purchase a property they plan to use during visits to South Africa.

The sale of the penthouse at The Marlow on Mill has set a new record for an apartment in Cape Town’s Southern Suburbs, highlighting continued demand for premium, well-located properties in the city.

UK buyers purchase Cape Town penthouse

According to Pam Golding Properties, the previous record for an apartment in the Southern Suburbs was R12.65 million, paid for a similar apartment at Newlands Peak when that development launched in 2020.



The latest sale therefore represents a significant jump in the price buyers are willing to pay for top-end sectional-title property in the area.

The buyers of the R15.9 million penthouse are based in the UK and intend to use the property as a home when visiting South Africa.

Their purchase reflects a wider trend at The Marlow on Mill, where interest has come from both South African and international buyers.

Foreign interest in the development has mainly come from buyers in the UK and US, with additional interest from Germany. The development has already recorded close to R350 million in sales.

Investors are driving sales

While the R15.9 million penthouse sale has attracted attention, investors are responsible for much of the development’s sales activity.

According to Pam Golding Properties, strong demand for both long- and short-term rentals is making the development attractive to buyers seeking rental income and potential capital growth.



Leisure buyers are also using the apartments as holiday homes, with the opportunity to let them out when they are not in Cape Town.

This combination of personal use and potential rental income is particularly appealing to buyers who live outside the city or overseas.

Who is buying at The Marlow on Mill?

According to sales stats, the development has attracted a mix of buyers from the Western Cape, other South African provinces, and overseas.

Around 70% of recent buyers are middle-aged or mature, while retirees and younger adults make up the remainder.

The foreign interest is particularly notable given the development’s location and the appeal of Cape Town to international property buyers.

The city offers these buyers a combination of natural scenery, established suburbs, lifestyle amenities and access to beaches, mountains, restaurants and cultural attractions.

World.title: NEW evidence emerges in sardine mortality investigation
World.content:
Laboratory testing has confirmed the presence of pilchard herpesvirus (PHV) genetic material in sardines linked to the recent mass mortality event along South Africa's West Coast. Image: canva

Laboratory testing has confirmed the presence of pilchard herpesvirus (PHV) genetic material in sardines linked to the recent mass mortality event along South Africa’s West Coast.

However, the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) says scientists have not yet established that the virus is responsible for the deaths.

PHV was detected in dead sardines and at lower levels in some apparently healthy fish collected from the West Coast. This suggests that the presence of the virus alone may not be sufficient to cause widespread mortality.



Scientists investigating environmental factors

Researchers are now investigating whether environmental conditions may have triggered or worsened the deaths.

Possible factors include harmful algal blooms, low oxygen levels and unusual oceanographic conditions.

These remain hypotheses and further evidence is needed before scientists can determine what caused the mortality event.

Testing of sardines collected from Saldanha Bay, the Cape Canyon and Gansbaai, as well as an apparently healthy comparison sample from St Helena Bay, found none of the paralytic toxins associated with harmful algal blooms in Saldanha Bay.

Low levels of two other algal toxins, domoic acid and yessotoxin, were detected. However, the highest concentrations were found in the apparently healthy comparison sample.

The department says the findings suggest the tested toxins were unlikely to have been the primary cause of the sardine deaths.



No evidence of risk to people

The department stressed that PHV is associated with sardines and there is currently no evidence that it infects humans or other animals.

The discovery of the virus also does not mean that commercially caught healthy sardines or canned sardine products are unsafe.

There is currently no general suspension of fishing or canning, although normal food-safety controls and monitoring will continue.

The public has nevertheless been warned not to collect or eat dead or dying sardines, or feed them to pets.

Urgent response planned

DFFE has convened an urgent briefing with representatives of the small pelagic fishing industry.

A task team involving the department, fishing industry and other stakeholders will be established to develop a coordinated response to the PHV-associated mortality.

Disease surveillance is also being expanded along South Africa’s West, South and East coasts, while additional disease, pathology and environmental investigations continue.

The department’s routine October/November hydroacoustic biomass survey will provide the first opportunity to assess whether the mortality event has had a measurable impact on the country’s sardine population.

PHV has not previously been reported in South African sardines, although it was associated with major sardine mortality events in Australasia during the 1990s. The virus was later detected in apparently healthy Australian sardine populations without causing ongoing mortality.

DFFE says it will provide further updates as the investigation progresses.

World.title: Banyana keep Brazil 2027 World Cup hopes alive
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa's Banyana Banyana kept their hopes alive of qualifying for the Women's World Cup Brazil year.

After defeating Nigeria 2-1 in their WAFCON play-in match, Banyana will serve as CAF's one of two teams alongside Ghana in the Play-Off's, which will be begin in November and December of this year and be completed in February 2027.

Ghana's Black Queens eliminated the Ivory Coast.

Both Ghana and South Africa will go through the first round of the playoffs, where they will face one of the following teams: Chinese Taipei, Uzbekistan, Ecuador, Venezuela, or Papua New Guinea.

At the end of this first phase, only two teams will qualify for the next round.

They will then face four nations from UEFA, Oceania Football C or CONMEBOL, who are exempt from the first round and qualified for the decisive phase.

The six teams who have won through to this phase will then be divided into three groups. In each group, a knockout match will determine the victor who will eventually book their spots to Brazil.

World.title: TikTok strangers rally to reunite Cape Town student with mother battling cancer
World.content:
PIETERMARITZBURG - What started as a tearful TikTok plea for strangers to visit her mother, who is being treated for cancer at a KwaZulu-Natal hospital, has turned into a remarkable story of kindness.

Earlier this week, Londiwe Molefe, originally from Newcastle, posted a tearful video on TikTok asking people to visit her mother at Greys Hospital in Pietermaritzburg.

Unable to afford the trip from Cape Town, Molefe said she feared her mother was not doing well and had no one else to check on her.

Her plea, which attracted more than 5,000 comments, struck a chord with the app's users.

“My mom was admitted at Greys Hospital. I’m currently in Cape Town and there is no one at home who can go check on her,” Molefe said in the video.

“I don’t have another option. She is not okay. If anyone is close to Greys or can visit her, please go. Even just five minutes with her would mean the world and make her feel so much better.”

Molefe’s followers responded to her plea, with one offering to buy her a plane ticket so she could travel to KwaZulu-Natal and be reunited with her mother. Many others flocked to Greys hospital to visit her mother.

On Wednesday, Molefe arrived in Pietermaritzburg and was also able to visit her mother. Another user also offered her a place to stay, while another good samaritan paid for her return ticket back to Cape Town.

Reflecting on the outpouring of support, Molefe thanked those who had donated, visited her mother on her behalf and offered emotional support.

“When I made the video about my mom being in hospital, I never imagined it would touch so many of you. Thank you for the donations. Thank you for going to see my mom on my behalf. Thank you for calling me, for the messages, for sacrificing your time,” she wrote.

“Because of your kindness, I am able to go to KZN to see my mom too. You carried me when I felt so broken. From the bottom of my heart, thank you.”

World.title: ‘A full-circle moment’: Gabi Motuba reflects on Standard Bank Joy of Jazz journey
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG – Standard Bank Young Artist winner Gabi Motuba says performing alongside American jazz vocalist Kurt Elling at the 2026 Standard Bank Joy of Jazz will be a full circle moment.

The Mamelodi-raised artist has been named among the top artists who serenade music lovers at this year’s festival set to take place on 25 and 26 September.

The lineup features global and South African stars including Floetry, Angélique Kidjo, McCoy Mrubata and Thandiswa Mazwai among others.

“It’s incredible. It’s quite surreal experience,” Motuba told eNCA.

“I remember going to one of the Joy of Jazz concerts and watching Kurt Elling, and now I’m on that very spot. It’s such a full circle moment for me because that was such a significant experience.”

Motuba will perform songs from her recent musical project Sounds from a Black Girl, which is a mix of neo soul and improvision.

“This offering is a meditation on affirmations. After coming from a sabbath themed around grief, I’m lucky to have come out on the other side. This is the tone of the album. I want it to arm young girls for a world that is not always accepting.”

World.title: 'Shock' gloves for US immigration agents fuel potential abuse fears
World.content:
WASHINGTON - Plans to equip US immigration enforcement agents with gloves capable of delivering debilitating electric shocks have fueled concerns over potential abuses by a force that critics say is already overzealous and under-trained.

"As if assaulting people and shooting people in the streets wasn't enough," Representative Maxwell Frost, a Democrat from Florida, said on X. "Now, they're spending $20 million of YOUR taxpayer dollars on painful electric shock gloves for their masked, lawless goons."

"ICE must be stopped," Frost said in a reference to Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the agency primarily charged with carrying out President Donald Trump's plan to deport millions of undocumented migrants.

ICE has come in for criticism for a series of fatal shootings during enforcement operations, including those of two American citizens in Minnesota in January who were involved in anti-ICE protests.

Critics have focused on the forceful tactics used by ICE agents in rounding up migrants and on an alleged lowering of the standards of training for new recruits.

The plan to purchase the shock gloves, which was first reported by The Associated Press, calls for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), the ICE parent agency, to spend $10 to $20 million on what are described as "distraction and de-escalation" devices.

The G.L.O.V.E., or Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter, is made by Compliant Technologies, a company based in Kentucky that bills itself on its website as a supplier of "cutting-edge non-lethal tools to empower and protect those who serve."

The G.L.O.V.E. delivers a shock that is not as strong as that of a Taser, another device used by law enforcement to subdue suspects.

In response to queries about the gloves, DHS said ICE is "constantly assessing the needs of our officers in the field to ensure they have the tools and equipment necessary to safely arrest and remove criminal illegal aliens from our country."

"Every decision is made with careful consideration and appropriately reviewed to ensure that any technology ICE utilises is consistent with all applicable law enforcement policies and standards," DHS said in a statement.

- 'Misused' -

John Sandweg, who served as the acting ICE director under Democratic president Barack Obama, said in an interview with MS NOW that ICE agents have an "incredibly difficult job" but expressed concerns about the electric gloves.

"Deploying this admittedly less-than-lethal technology, in an era when we're really not all that interested in providing training to the officers about how to use that technology, really is alarming," Sandweg said.

"It doesn't take a big stretch of the imagination to see this technology being deployed against a mother who's just maybe putting up the mildest resistance because she's being separated from her children," he said. "It's too easy for this to get misused against a population that doesn't pose a threat."

Representative Pramila Jayapal, a Democrat from Washington state, expressed similar concerns.

"ICE has targeted legal observers, protestors, and just ordinary people on their way to work or to drop their kid off at school," Jayapal said on X. "This won't make anyone safer and in fact just gives ICE another dangerous tool to target citizens and immigrants alike."

The American Civil Liberties Union announced last month that it has filed more than 50 claims against the federal government on behalf of people and families allegedly harmed by federal immigration actions in 17 states and in Washington, the nation's capital.

ICE arrested more than 51,000 people for immigration violations across the country in July, according to US media reports citing DHS sources, the most in a single month since Trump took office in January of last year.

World.title: Trump announces tariffs of up to 100% on imported drones
World.content:
WASHINGTON - President Donald Trump announced on Thursday tariffs of up to 100 percent on imports of unmanned drones and their components to reduce US reliance on imports in an industry dominated by China.

The US president justified the decision on national security grounds, according to a White House statement that detailed a 100 percent duty rate on the import of certain unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), as they are formally known.

Those with a takeoff weight of more than 25 kilograms and with so-called national security capabilities such as thermal cameras and docking stations will be tariffed at 100 percent.

Smaller drones face a 25 percent tariff.

The statement said the tariffs will "encourage increased domestic production" of drones and their components and reduce reliance on foreign supply chains.

Most of the new tariffs are to take effect September 3.

"The tariffs are really targeting industrial and commercial drones, and to a lesser degree smaller drones used by hobbyists," Clayton Swope, a senior fellow at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, told AFP.

- Dual use -

In December 2025, the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) -- which is charged with regulating telecommunications nationally -- argued that domestic production of drones would "reduce the risk of direct UAS attacks and disruptions, unauthorised surveillance, sensitive data exfiltration, and other UAS threats to the homeland."

It added that drones "are inherently dual-use: they are both commercial platforms and potentially military or paramilitary sensors and weapons," and foreign production of drones and their components, "could enable persistent surveillance, data exfiltration, and destructive operations over US territory."

The war in Ukraine has underscored how commercial and hobbyist drones can be outfitted for frontline attacks.

The Chinese company DJI, founded in 2006, has captured more than two-thirds of the global drone market in recent years, according to several studies.

It has also been in Washington's crosshairs for several years, with US officials accusing it of supplying products used to surveil ethnic minorities in China, particularly the Uyghurs.

Since 2022, DJI has been on a US list of Chinese companies linked to the country's military and therefore subject to restrictions on access to US technology.

DJI fought its inclusion on the list in 2024, insisting that it was not owned or controlled by the military.

It is "critical that America be able to produce its own unmanned capabilities without parts or even raw materials from China," Joshua Steinman, a supply chain expert formerly on the Trump administration's National Security Council, told AFP.

Last week, China announced restrictions on drone exports to the United States and blacklisted six companies in response to trade sanctions imposed by Washington over forced labour and national security concerns.

That move came days after the US imposed fresh tariffs on China and 59 countries.

In late July 2026, the US government also added humanoid and quadruped robots to a blacklist of products and companies barred from import into the United States, saying they posed critical national security risks.

That sector, too, is dominated by Chinese industry.

World.title: Europe swelters under fresh wave of extreme heat
World.content:
PARIS - Millions of people across Europe -- particularly in France, Italy, Spain and Britain -- baked through a new wave of extreme temperatures Thursday as the continent's latest heatwave picked up.

More than 135 million people were forecast to face temperatures above 35C, with Britain recording its fifth-hottest day on record and parts of France soaring past 42C.
